docs.title: Linha documentation
docs.text:
Linha lets an application submit work now and retrieve the outcome later. A job ID remains useful across application, server and worker restarts. You provide business code in a worker image; Linha records requests and manages the engine.

These pages serve application developers and Kubernetes operators equally.

Development version

These pages follow the current source checkout. Source builds use 0.1.3-SNAPSHOT; choose a release in the version selector for documentation matching published artifacts.

I want to… Start here Try Linha locally Run your first job Write a job and submit it Build a Scala client and worker Deploy an HA server Deploy on Kubernetes Connect an application securely Configure OAuth 2.0 client credentials Configure Spark resources and scaling Manage Spark applications Inspect contexts and replay requests Enable the administrator console Build a Grafana view Monitor queries and resources Find a field or endpoint Configuration, SDK, HTTP API Understand durability and context lifetime Architecture

docs.title: Learn, operate, look up, understand
docs.text:
Tutorials walk through a working outcome. How-to guides solve a specific operational or development task. Reference pages list contracts and defaults. Explanation pages describe why the system behaves as it does.

The documentation site keeps a development version and independent release snapshots. Existing snapshots remain available when the development docs change. Release notes describe the behavior of earlier releases.

docs.title: Measured fixtures
docs.text:
A fixture with 25,000 retained jobs and 120 logical contexts produced 3,945 series under the default 100 named dimensions plus overflow. Snapshot collection took 23.3 ms and a 50-context admin page took 1.3 ms. Eight concurrent callers performed 80 cached scrapes in 48.1 ms without acquiring a database connection.

The Overview query returned complete counts and five context details in 13.2 ms under the race build on that host. These are observed fixture values; histogram population, hardware and production data distributions can change them.

The disposable Spark fixture used two API replicas, two drivers with two request slots each and 0–2 executors per driver. Observed executors grew to four and returned to zero. Lost applications were replaced and retired UI URLs disappeared. Edited replay succeeded; cancellation preserved unrelated requests.

docs.title: Failure behavior
docs.text:
• Pausing PostgreSQL made both servers unready. /metrics still returned local data and omitted unavailable shared families.
  • Revoking Kubernetes reads produced forbidden API metrics and stale observations; restoration recovered fresh totals.
  • Removing a published local file returned an explicit storage failure without deleting its metadata; restoring the file recovered retrieval.
  • Losing an accepting replica after commit and retrying the same request returned one job ID and one acceptance audit entry.
  • Full server restart preserved the accounting ledger; queued/running work recovered and cancellation remained authoritative.

Run the repository scripts, including check-observability.py, admin-spark-e2e.py and admin-observability-e2e.py, for the corresponding fixtures. Raw output and exact environment identifiers are omitted from the public record.

docs.title: Enable the administrator console
docs.text:
The console displays contexts, clients, workers, requests, attempts and retained results. Operators can create or edit-and-replay requests, cancel accepted work and move pending requests to a corrected context version. It is embedded in the server image and disabled by default.

This guide assumes a reachable Linha server and an OIDC provider. API OAuth configuration remains independent; see client authentication.

docs.title: 1. Register a browser client
docs.text:
Create a separate OpenID Connect client, such as linha-admin, using authorization code with PKCE. Register the exact callback URL:

https://linha.example/ui/oidc/callback

Use the provider's issuer URL for security.oidc.issuer. If the browser client is confidential, store its secret in a Secret in the release namespace. A public client can omit ui.oidc.secretRef.

docs.title: 2. Configure administrator groups
docs.text:
Add a provider mapper that includes group membership in the ID token. Match the exact emitted values, including any group path prefix. For example:

security:
  oidc:
    enabled: true
    issuer: https://identity.example/realms/jobs
  admin:
    viewer:
      claims:
        - path: [groups]
          values: [linha-viewers]
    operator:
      claims:
        - path: [groups]
          values: [linha-operators]
ui:
  enabled: true
  publicURL: https://linha.example/ui/
  sessionSeconds: 3600
  oidc:
    clientId: linha-admin
    scopes: [openid, profile, email, groups]
    secretRef: linha-browser-client
    clientSecretKey: client-secret

Add a groups scope only if the provider supports it. Alternatively attach a default group mapper and use the provider's ordinary browser scopes. Keycloak's Group Membership mapper can emit a claim such as groups; configure Add to ID token and choose whether values include full group paths.

Rules belong under security.admin, alongside security.oidc. They inherit the browser issuer; do not repeat it. Claim paths support nested objects and values that are strings or arrays of strings. Operators can also view. No administrator is granted access by default.

docs.title: 3. Expose the same origin
docs.text:
ui:
  publicURL: https://linha.example/ui/
  ingress:
    enabled: true
    className: nginx
    tls:
      enabled: true
      secretName: linha-ui-tls

Install the ingress controller, configure DNS and provide its TLS Secret. The chart infers the host from ui.publicURL and routes /ui and /v1/admin to the existing Service. Preserve these paths; no rewriting or sticky sessions are required. If TLS terminates upstream, retain the external HTTPS public URL and set ingress TLS to false. An externally managed ingress can use the same routes.

docs.title: 4. Verify the console
docs.text:
• Overview: current work, capacity, health and recent activity.
  • Contexts: logical names and immutable versions, clients with hostnames, worker instances, current allocations and separated historical observations.
  • Requests: payloads, state, progress, attempts, failures, cancellation and links to retained results. Edit-and-replay opens the create form.
  • Servers: replica readiness, versions and heartbeat freshness.
  • Create request: select a context version, edit JSON, set policy and submit.

Spark instances link to a current UI ingress when the SparkApplication exposes one. Otherwise use the displayed service/port and port forwarding. Historical instances do not imply that their UI is still reachable.

File results expose names, sizes, digests and locations, with bounded previews when supported. Dataset parts are paginated. Operators have actions; viewers have inspection access. Actions are recorded in the persisted audit history.

docs.title: Recover a stranded queue
docs.text:
Use this procedure when an old context version is draining but its workers cannot start. First ensure that the corrected version has working workers and supports the queued handlers and payload contracts.

  1. Open Requests, or open the old context version and choose its Requests tab.
  2. Use the context suggestions and local date/time inputs to locate the work.
  3. Select the queued or retrying requests. The header checkbox selects eligible rows on the current page; repeat for further pages as needed.
  4. Choose Move selected, search the destination versions, and choose the corrected active version. Confirm the move.
  5. Review Batch results. Successful rows move immediately; failed rows remain selected with an explanation. Refresh and retry those rows if appropriate.

The destination must have the same owner, logical context name, engine type and engine version. It must retain the source's workload storage destinations and fingerprints. Stopped and draining versions cannot receive moved work.

A move preserves public request IDs, payloads, submission time, deadline, retry count/backoff and the original result-storage policy. Clients keep polling the same IDs. The source can finish draining once its remaining accepted work ends. Each actual move appears in the request's administrative audit with links to the source and destination versions.

Running requests cannot move. Choose Cancel selected to signal running work or cancel pending work; cancellation leaves drivers available for other requests. If a payload needs editing, use Edit and replay to create a new request and cancel the obsolete request instead of moving it unchanged.

Batch actions apply per request. A worker can claim a row while the dialog is open; that row then reports a conflict instead of being executed twice. The API accepts up to 200 unique IDs per batch; the UI selects one page at a time. See the OpenAPI contract for POST /v1/admin/jobs/batch.

docs.title: Keep browser sessions connected
docs.text:
Linha renews short-lived identity credentials on the server when the provider issues a refresh token. Refresh credentials remain encrypted in PostgreSQL; JavaScript and browser cookies never contain provider tokens. Any replica can renew the same session, and current administrator membership is checked again.

Set the maximum browser session duration explicitly. For example, for eight hours:

ui:
  sessionSeconds: 28800

The default is 3600 seconds; the supported range is 60–86400 seconds. Renewal does not extend this absolute limit. The provider's own session expiry or revocation can end access earlier. Sign in once after upgrading: sessions created by older servers have no refresh credential and retain their original expiry.

For Keycloak, enable the browser client's Standard flow and align its client and realm session timeouts with the duration you need. Ordinary interactive renewal does not require offline_access. Other providers may require an extra scope or consent to issue a refresh token; use ui.oidc.scopes when needed. If refreshed ID tokens are omitted, Linha uses fresh UserInfo and verifies its subject, so UserInfo must include the claims used by administrator mappings. See the Keycloak session documentation and OpenID Connect refresh rules.

A temporary provider outage does not extend an expired identity. Rejected refresh credentials, changed identity, removed administrator membership, or an interrupted provider-token rotation can require another login. Logout removes the shared session so another replica cannot revive it.

docs.title: Diagnose login
docs.text:
Symptom Check Provider rejects the callback Exact registered callback, browser client flow and PKCE settings administrator role required security.admin location, emitted ID-token claim path and exact group values Groups missing Provider mapper includes the ID token; requested scope is supported Invalid audience Browser ID token targets ui.oidc.clientId, not API audience linha Certificate error Provider CA trusted by server and browser; these are separate trust stores Login needed at each short token expiry Sign in after upgrading; verify the provider issues a refresh token and the browser client can refresh Login needed at a fixed longer interval Check ui.sessionSeconds and the provider's maximum session duration

Log in again after changing scopes or the provider's token mapper. Administrator mappings are evaluated using the running server configuration on every request. The browser session is database-backed, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax and Secure over HTTPS. Its absolute lifetime is bounded by ui.sessionSeconds. Without a refresh token, it also ends at identity-token expiry. JavaScript never stores bearer tokens.

For an isolated development fixture, security.enabled: false with ui.enabled: true gives anonymous operator access. It provides no user isolation.

docs.title: Access application files through Linha
docs.text: Application storage is for input files, shared datasets and temporary processing files. It is separate from a job's published result. Linha result expiration never removes application files.

docs.title: Enable a destination
docs.text:
An operator configures a named S3 destination on the server with allowWorkloadAccess: true:

{
  "application-data": {
    "bucket": "application-bucket",
    "prefix": "processing",
    "region": "eu-west-1",
    "endpoint": "http://object-storage.storage.svc:9000",
    "pathStyle": true,
    "allowWorkloadAccess": true
  }
}

The server obtains S3 credentials through its normal AWS credential chain. Give it read, list, put, copy and delete permissions on the configured prefix. Application access is disabled unless explicitly enabled. Use a dedicated destination/prefix for each trust boundary: an authorized context requesting a destination can access that entire prefix, including shared application files written by other contexts using it.

The client's backend configuration requests access by name:

"storage": { "destinations": ["application-data"] }

Linha snapshots the physical destination fingerprint into the context version. Moving the destination to another bucket, prefix or endpoint prevents old sessions from accessing the new location.

docs.title: Upload an input from the client
docs.text:
val context = Await.result(client.ensureBackend("processing", backend), Duration.Inf)
val storage = Await.result(context.storage("application-data"), Duration.Inf)
try storage.upload("inputs/source.nc", Paths.get("source.nc"))
finally storage.close()

A client session depends on the context's live client attachment. Reacquire a session if that attachment expires; a session token alone cannot revive it. Session tokens are scoped bearer credentials. Keep them out of durable job payloads, logs and public URLs. Send the destination name and application paths in the request instead.

docs.title: Read and write in a worker
docs.text:
val storage = ctx.storage("application-data")
val input = storage.open("inputs/source.nc")
try process(input)
finally input.close()

A worker session is bound to the active job attempt, worker incarnation and fence. The server checks its current database lease on each operation. Completion, cancellation, worker replacement and lease expiry deny subsequent access. PostgreSQL stores token digests, allowing another server replica to serve the same session after a restart.

For Spark or another Hadoop client, add com.k3rnl:linha-hadoop_2.12 and propagate the session's Hadoop options before creating a dataset or RDD:

storage.hadoopOptions.foreach { case (key, value) =>
  spark.sparkContext.hadoopConfiguration.set(key, value)
}
val path = storage.path("datasets/output") // linha://<session-id>/datasets/output
frame.write.parquet(path)

Executors use the same scoped session through the Linha HTTP gateway. They receive no S3 access keys and need no application Secret, ConfigMap or shared PVC. Credentials use session-specific option names, so concurrent sessions remain separate. Redact token configuration keys in Spark logs and UI. Only delegate sessions to trusted executors.

The filesystem supports seekable range reads, create/overwrite, listing, directories, rename and delete. Append is unsupported. Rename uses S3 copy/delete and is not atomic. Directory operations are limited to 10,000 objects, uploads to 5 GiB per object. Hadoop writes stage on the worker's temporary disk; server uploads reserve space against maxStagingBytes. Size both disks and server bandwidth for the expected file sizes and concurrency. Storage traffic passes through Linha rather than directly between executors and S3.

docs.title: Serialize shared metadata updates
docs.text:
val lock = storage.lock("datasets/example/index")
try updateSharedIndex(storage)
finally lock.close()

Locks are 30-second PostgreSQL leases renewed by the SDK. All sessions addressing the same physical destination and directory contend on the same key. SDK writes below the locked directory include a lock proof; Linha verifies it and holds the lock row during publication. A writer that loses the lock cannot begin another protected write.

Locks do not make arbitrary S3 side effects exactly once. A request already executing against S3 when cancellation arrives may finish. Keep output operations repeatable and choose retry/replay policies appropriate for your application.

docs.title: Return status without an artifact
docs.text:
A Scala entrypoint returning Unit registers a status result descriptor. On success the worker commits an empty file list; no allocation or result upload occurs. Raw handlers return StatusResult with a matching descriptor. Clients can still retrieve the durable job state, progress and failure, and typed result() returns Unit after success.

Application owners manage retention of staged inputs, scratch and datasets, for example through S3 lifecycle policies. Keep inputs if administrators must replay requests later, and clean per-attempt scratch before completion while its storage session remains valid.

docs.title: How Linha works
docs.text: Linha separates durable job management from engine execution. Clients send JSON; PostgreSQL owns requests, attempts and leases; workers run business code and publish results through Linha's storage policy.

docs.title: Acceptance and execution
docs.text:
The server returns an opaque job ID after committing acceptance to PostgreSQL. A driver need not be ready yet. A later worker claims an attempt and renews its lease while it executes. Progress and completion are accepted only for the current attempt and worker identity.

An idempotency key makes repeated acceptance safe. The same owner, logical context name, key, request and result policy return the original job. Reusing the key with different content is a conflict. It does not make arbitrary external business writes exactly-once. Execution retries are separate and disabled by default.

docs.title: Context names and versions
docs.text:
A context is an owner's logical workload, such as reporting. A version records its effective engine settings, result policy, Pod templates and resolved worker image digest. Linha normalizes and hashes these values; callers do not add version suffixes to the context name.

Each application process leases the version it uses. SDK leases last 90 seconds and renew every 30 seconds. Old and new versions can coexist during a rolling update. When the final client releases its lease or disappears, the version drains: it finishes accepted work, then stops its drivers. minDrivers does not keep an unused drained version alive. A stuck accepted job can delay draining until it finishes or is cancelled.

Restoring a job handle does not attach to a context or start an engine. Reading retained results requires only the same authenticated owner and job ID.

docs.title: Spark concurrency and capacity
docs.text:
A driver owns one classic SparkContext. Each request receives a separate SparkSession, scheduler pool and attempt-specific job group. Several requests can run at once, bounded by maxConcurrentRequestsPerDriver; cancellation targets one job group. Spark executor slots still determine how much task work runs in parallel.

Linha scales the driver pool within the requested bounds and replaces lost required drivers. Spark independently manages executors through dynamic allocation. A worker interruption can fail or retry an attempt according to the accepted retry policy. Replacing a driver alone does not guarantee that a job is retried.

docs.title: Result publication and retention
docs.text:
JSON, files and datasets use the context's local or S3 policy. A completed write is not yet a public result: the current attempt must complete successfully. Dataset parts are copied into immutable published allocations before they are exposed. Late writers and stale attempts cannot replace the retained result.

Job IDs and status remain after result payload expiry. Retrieval then returns RESULT_EXPIRED. Optional physical cleanup removes only eligible tracked allocations; it does not delete job history or arbitrary bucket contents.

docs.title: Authentication boundaries
docs.text:
Connection Identity and purpose Application → API OAuth 2.0 client credentials; signed JWT access token with audience linha Browser → administrator console OIDC authorization code with PKCE; browser client audience and explicit viewer/operator claims Managed worker → server Bound Kubernetes service-account token, checked against the live managed instance Server → PostgreSQL/S3/Kubernetes Deployment credentials managed by the operator

The issuer identifies who issued a token. The audience identifies the service it was issued for. Signature validation alone does not establish that the token was intended for Linha. All callers can share the linha audience while retaining distinct subjects and owner-isolated job records.

Administrator roles apply only to the separate admin surface. Worker credentials are injected into managed worker Pods; they are unrelated to application OAuth client secrets and must not be removed when simplifying application authentication.

docs.title: Availability boundaries
docs.text: Multiple server replicas share PostgreSQL locks, persisted controller intent and sessions. Restarts preserve accepted jobs, result references and client leases. The Helm chart cannot make a single database, object store or local disk highly available. Use durable infrastructure and test failures appropriate to the target environment. Authorized worker images execute with namespace permissions and shared storage access, so deployments should group workloads by their trust boundary.

docs.title: Configure OAuth 2.0 client credentials
docs.text:
Use an OAuth 2.0 service client to authenticate an application to Linha. The SDK obtains and replaces access tokens itself. Mount the OAuth client secret, not a pre-generated JWT. No token file or identity-provider-specific login adapter is required.

This guide assumes an OAuth authorization server that issues signed JWT access tokens and publishes OIDC discovery and signing keys. Linha does not accept opaque access tokens. For the identity model, see authentication boundaries.

docs.title: 1. Register an application identity
docs.text:
Create a confidential client with the client_credentials grant enabled. Give every independent application its own client ID and secret. Replicas of the same application should share that identity so they can retrieve the same jobs.

Configure the access token's audience to include linha. This is the identity of the target API; it is shared by all applications calling Linha. The client ID identifies the caller and does not replace this audience.

Find the exact issuer and token endpoint in the provider's discovery document. The issuer URL and token endpoint serve different purposes.

docs.title: 2. Configure Linha's API verifier
docs.text:
security:
  enabled: true
  api:
    enabled: true
    jwt:
      issuer: https://identity.example/realms/jobs
      audience: linha
      tls:
        insecureSkipVerify: false

Linha checks the token signature, issuer, audience, expiry and nonempty subject. Owners are derived from the verified issuer and subject. A correctly signed token intended for another service is rejected.

Browser administrator login is separate: it uses security.oidc, ui.oidc.clientId and security.admin. API tokens do not automatically grant administrator access. See enable the console.

docs.title: 3. Construct the SDK provider
docs.text:
Install the development SDKs from this checkout with Java 17 mvn -B install.

Use the matching client and protocol artifacts:

import linha.CredentialProvider
import linha.client.LinhaClient
import linha.client.auth.CredentialProviders
import java.nio.file.Paths
import scala.concurrent.ExecutionContext.Implicits.global

val credentials = CredentialProviders.oauthClientCredentials(
  tokenEndpoint = "https://identity.example/realms/jobs/protocol/openid-connect/token",
  clientId = "reporting-api",
  clientSecret = CredentialProvider.fileSecret(Paths.get("/credentials/client-secret")),
  scopes = Seq.empty
)
val client = new LinhaClient("https://linha.example", credentials)

The secret supplier is called when a token is acquired, so a refreshed Secret file can be used without restarting the SDK. The SDK sends HTTP Basic client authentication and grant_type=client_credentials. Request scopes only when the provider requires them; openid is not required by Linha's machine API.

The provider is shared by job submission, context heartbeats, status polling and result downloads. Keep it, the client and its contexts for the application process lifetime. Close the client during graceful shutdown.

docs.title: 4. Check the Keycloak settings
docs.text:
For Keycloak, enable Client authentication and Service accounts roles on an OpenID Connect client. Create an audience mapper or client scope that adds linha to the access token audience. Attach that scope to each service client that may call Linha. The service-account subject gives each client a distinct owner.

Typical URLs are:

Issuer:         https://identity.example/realms/jobs
Token endpoint: https://identity.example/realms/jobs/protocol/openid-connect/token

An installation configured with a context path might include /auth before /realms. Use the URLs in discovery rather than guessing the path. The realm URL alone is not a token endpoint. Keycloak documents service accounts and audiences.

docs.title: 5. Configure TLS when needed
docs.text:
For a private CA, mount its PEM file and configure this one provider:

import linha.client.auth.IdentityHttpOptions

val options = IdentityHttpOptions(
  caFile = Some(Paths.get("/credentials/identity-ca.crt"))
)

Pass options = options to oauthClientCredentials. Verification is enabled by default. insecureSkipVerify = true explicitly skips certificate and hostname verification for this provider only. allowHttp = true permits HTTP for an isolated fixture. Neither option changes TLS settings for the Linha HTTP transport.

docs.title: Refresh and failure behavior
docs.text:
Tokens refresh on the next SDK call near expiry; active context heartbeats also make those calls. Concurrent requests share one acquisition. If refresh fails, an unexpired cached token can still be used, with a five-second acquisition backoff. An expired token is never returned. Credentials need no background thread.

Errors report the operation and, when available, the HTTP status. They exclude provider response bodies, tokens and secrets. The SDK does not retry a job mutation automatically after an authentication failure.

For defaults and limits, see SDK credential reference. For 401 and 403 diagnosis, see job and authentication failures.

docs.title: Compatibility matrix
docs.text:
These versions define the tested baseline, rather than a promise that every newer or older dependency combination works.

Component Baseline Server/toolchain Go 1.27.1, Linux amd64 SDK Scala 2.12.20, Java 17, Maven 3.9.9 Spark Classic Spark 3.5.6, Scala 2.12 Spark Operator Kubeflow 2.4.0, SparkApplication v1beta2 PostgreSQL 16/17, schema 10 Web build Node.js 22.12+, React/TypeScript with committed lockfile Cluster fixture Kubernetes 1.33.1, Kind Result storage Shared POSIX filesystem, AWS S3 API tested with MinIO Monitoring fixture Prometheus 3.7.1 / Operator 0.94.1; Grafana 13.2.3 / Operator 5.25.0 S3 connectors Hadoop AWS 3.3.4, AWS SDK bundle 1.12.262, Spark Hadoop Cloud 3.5.6 Documentation MkDocs 1.6.1, Material 9.7.7, mike 2.2.0

The protocol is JSON and independent of Scala binary versions. The current JVM artifacts target Scala 2.12; Scala 2.13 or 3 requires compatible bindings and Spark libraries. Do not mix Spark/Hadoop connector versions arbitrarily.

The example assembly shades Cats, Circe, Jawn and Shapeless to avoid conflicts with Spark's bundled dependencies. Spark is provided by the image rather than bundled into the application JAR. Preserve equivalent isolation in custom images.

The image retains Spark's native driver/executor entrypoint and contains the JAR named in application.mainApplicationFile. Linha does not transfer business code from the client at submission.

Database migrations are serialized through a PostgreSQL advisory lock. Current schema 10 includes dataset metadata, observations, durable accounting, admin sessions/audit, hostnames and overview indexes. Older server binaries reject newer schemas; additive migration does not imply arbitrary binary rollback.

docs.title: Configuration reference
docs.text:
Configuration belongs to three surfaces: deployment settings in Helm, immutable backend settings supplied by the client, and policy captured with each request. Unknown or conflicting fields are rejected rather than silently ignored.

The complete chart contract is in values.yaml and values.schema.json.

The removed existingSecret, deploymentMode, top-level oidc, and security.oidc.audience fields are not part of the current contract.

docs.title: Spark settings
docs.text:
These fields are under spec.engine.settings. The engine type is spark, version 3.5.6. The application uses sparkoperator.k8s.io/v1beta2.

Field Type / default Contract application.mainClass string / required JVM main class installed in the image application.mainApplicationFile string / required local:/// path ending in .jar application.arguments string array / [] At most 128 main-class arguments drivers.minDrivers integer / 1 Minimum with demand, may be zero drivers.maxDrivers integer / 1 1–16, at least the minimum drivers.maxConcurrentRequestsPerDriver integer / 1 1–32 request slots per driver drivers.queueThreshold integer / 1 Ready queue threshold for scale-up drivers.waitSeconds integer / 5 Queue wait threshold for scale-up drivers.cooldownSeconds integer / 10 Scale-up cooldown drivers.idleSeconds integer / 60 Idle retirement above minimum drivers.cores, executors.cores integer / 1 Spark parallelism, 1–32 drivers.coreRequest, executors.coreRequest quantity string / cores Positive CPU request, up to 32 cores drivers.coreLimit, executors.coreLimit quantity string / cores CPU limit, at least request, up to 32 cores drivers.memory, executors.memory string / 1024m JVM heap, 512m–128g, units m/g drivers.memoryOverhead, executors.memoryOverhead string / max(384m, 10% heap) Added to heap for container request and limit drivers.javaOptions, executors.javaOptions string / empty Additional JVM options; heap overrides rejected executors.dynamicAllocation boolean / false Spark executor autoscaling executors.instances integer / 1 Static executor count, 1–128 executors.minExecutors integer / 0 Dynamic minimum executors.initialExecutors integer / 1 Dynamic startup count, at least minimum executors.maxExecutors integer / 4 Dynamic maximum, at least initial, 1–128 executors.executorIdleTimeout duration / 60s Idle timeout without retained data executors.cachedExecutorIdleTimeout duration / infinity Cached-data retention timeout executors.shuffleTrackingTimeout duration / infinity Shuffle-data retention timeout ui.enabled boolean / false Start each driver's Spark UI ui.port integer / 4040 1024–65535 kubernetes.driverPodTemplate, executorPodTemplate objects / empty Independent native fragments; each at most 64 KiB

Durations accept positive integer s/m/h/d units up to 2,147,483,647 seconds. Cache/shuffle timeouts also accept infinity. Equivalent durations normalize to one configuration version. Deprecated memoryMi is a heap alias and cannot be combined with memory; new configuration should use Spark units.

Example: memory: "10g" with memoryOverhead: "2g" creates a 10g heap inside a 12Gi container. See manage Spark applications.

docs.title: Results and request policy
docs.text:
Field Default / bound Meaning results.type local or s3 Backend result provider results.root allowed configured root Local result filesystem results.destination configured alias S3 destination; no bucket credentials in requests results.path version 1 template Relative output key policy retry.maxAttempts 1, maximum 10 Total attempts, including the first retry.backoffSeconds 1 Delay between eligible retries Result maxBytes 64 MiB, maximum 5 GiB Total accepted result bytes Result retention seven days by default Availability duration; metadata remains after expiry Attempt lease 30 seconds Current worker authority Client lease 90 seconds Context demand; SDK renews every 30 seconds Dataset parts maximum 100,000 Distributed output inventory cap

The OpenAPI contract is authoritative for complete request schema, policy placement and bounds.

docs.title: Result path templates
docs.text:
The default is {contextId}/{requestId}/{attemptId}/{file}. {requestId} and {attemptId} must each occupy a complete segment, and {file} must appear once at the end. {contextId} is optional. {submittedAt} expands the original accepted time in UTC; formats allow yyyy/MM/dd/HH/mm/ss/SSS fields and / - _ T Z literals.

exports/{submittedAt:yyyy/MM/dd}/{requestId}/{attemptId}/{file}

Templates are declarative data, not remote lambdas. Absolute paths, URI schemes, traversal, encoded traversal and reserved _linha segments are rejected. The S3 bucket and base prefix remain administrator-controlled.

docs.title: Standalone server environment
docs.text:
Helm field Environment variable Master security LINHA_SECURITY_ENABLED API JWT enabled / issuer / audience LINHA_API_AUTH_ENABLED, LINHA_API_JWT_ISSUER, LINHA_API_JWT_AUDIENCE API provider TLS bypass LINHA_API_JWT_TLS_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY Browser OIDC enabled / issuer LINHA_OIDC_ENABLED, LINHA_OIDC_ISSUER Browser provider TLS bypass LINHA_OIDC_TLS_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY Admin membership JSON LINHA_ADMIN_MAPPINGS Browser client / scopes LINHA_UI_OIDC_CLIENT_ID, LINHA_UI_OIDC_SCOPES Database fields LINHA_DATABASE_HOST, PORT, NAME, USERNAME, PASSWORD, SSL_MODE, SSL_ROOT_CERT, each with LINHA_DATABASE_ prefix Cleanup / staging LINHA_CLEANUP_ENABLED, LINHA_MAX_STAGING_BYTES Worker templates / pull names / permitted registry names LINHA_WORKER_POD_TEMPLATES, LINHA_WORKER_IMAGE_PULL_SECRETS, LINHA_REGISTRY_SECRETS

A standalone LINHA_DATABASE_URL is mutually exclusive with separate database fields. Managed backends also require LINHA_SERVER_URL, LINHA_WORKER_SERVICE_ACCOUNT and LINHA_ALLOWED_IMAGES. Helm supplies these. LINHA_WORKER_AUTH selects projected-token (default) or token-review. Use JSON arrays/objects for structured environment settings.

docs.title: Return files and Spark datasets
docs.text:
The context selects local or S3 storage. Business code returns JSON, FileResult or DatasetResult; the SDK allocates output and publishes it after successful completion. The return type does not contain a bucket or storage-specific marker.

This guide assumes a registered typed Spark entrypoint and a result destination. See the client/worker tutorial for that setup.

docs.title: Return a stream or file
docs.text:
From an entrypoint returning FileResult:

ctx.results.stream("summary.csv", "text/csv") { output =>
  output.write("rows\n1000\n".getBytes("UTF-8"))
}

Use a temporary seekable path when a library needs one:

ctx.results.file("report.bin", "application/octet-stream") { path =>
  java.nio.file.Files.write(path, Array[Byte](1, 2, 3))
}

A failing callback does not publish its output. Stream helpers bound bytes while writing; seekable callbacks are checked after returning. Use an ephemeral-storage quota when third-party writes need a hard disk bound.

docs.title: Return distributed Parquet
docs.text:
import linha._
import linha.json._
import linha.spark._
import linha.spark.syntax._

final case class ExportRows(size: Long) extends SparkEntrypoint[DatasetResult] {
  def execute(ctx: LinhaJobContext[Spark]): DatasetResult = {
    val frame = ctx.spark.range(size).selectExpr("id", "id % 2 AS group")
    ctx.results.parquet(frame, "events", partitionBy = Seq("group"))
  }
}
object ExportRows {
  implicit val codec = EntrypointCodec.derived[ExportRows, DatasetResult]("export-rows", 1)
}

Executors write parts without collecting the DataFrame to the driver. The helper inventories and hashes each committed part. Publication verifies and copies the parts into immutable allocations. This requires extra I/O and storage but protects retained results from late writers. Registration or sealing alone does not publish.

docs.title: Configure local storage
docs.text:
Mount the same durable filesystem at the configured result root in every server, driver and executor. Use group-writable directories compatible with group 10001. A server-created marker is checked by Spark tasks; a missing or different mount fails the write instead of producing inaccessible worker-local data.

val storage = linha.client.ResultStorage.Local("/var/lib/linha/results")

Linha does not provision the filesystem. See deployment.

docs.title: Configure S3 dataset delegation
docs.text:
JSON and ordinary files use server-authorized uploads. Distributed S3 datasets also require STS AssumeRole with enforced session policies:

{
  "analytics": {
    "bucket": "example-results",
    "prefix": "linha",
    "region": "eu-west-1",
    "datasetRoleArn": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/linha-datasets"
  }
}

The server's AWS credentials must be allowed to assume that role. Its base policy allows the configured result prefix; the delegated session policy narrows writes to one staging allocation. For compatible stores, add endpoint, stsEndpoint and pathStyle. A provider without the necessary STS support returns DATASET_UNSUPPORTED, while file output remains available.

Grants last at most one hour, with no transparent renewal during a write. Credentials stay in per-write Hadoop configuration, with filesystem caching disabled. The helper uses S3A magic committers. Include matching connector JARs in the worker image:

scripts/prepare-spark-connectors.sh
mvn -B package
docker build -f examples/spark/Dockerfile -t registry.example/workers/example:1 .

The pinned example uses Hadoop AWS 3.3.4, AWS SDK bundle 1.12.262 and Spark Hadoop Cloud 3.5.6. See compatibility, Hadoop committers and STS session policies.

docs.title: Retrieve retained output
docs.text:
val handle = client.job(savedJobId, ExportRows.codec)
val result = Await.result(handle.result(), 30.seconds)
val manifest = result.dataset.get
val page = Await.result(handle.parts(limit = 100), 30.seconds)
Await.result(handle.download(manifest.manifest.allocationId, manifestFile), 30.seconds)
Await.result(handle.downloadPart("group=0/part-....parquet", partFile), 30.seconds)

This continues the client setup from the tutorial. Use the returned nextCursor to enumerate further pages. Use part paths verbatim, rather than constructing S3 keys. All downloads pass through Linha and authorize the current owner anew; the job ID is not an expiring S3 URL.

docs.title: Bound storage and enable cleanup
docs.text:
Default result size is 64 MiB, with a 5 GiB maximum. The dataset cap is 100,000 parts; SDK registration batches contain at most 100 parts. Manifest bytes are also bounded. Server and worker staging reservations default to 5 GiB.

results:
  maxStagingBytes: 5368709120
  cleanup:
    enabled: true

Physical cleanup is disabled by default. When enabled it waits for terminal attempts, delegated-write expiry and ten minutes of grace, and removes only tracked allocations that are not protected by retained results. It aborts eligible abandoned multipart uploads under those prefixes. Result expiry applies even when physical cleanup is disabled. Job IDs, receipts and idempotency records remain as metadata. External lifecycle rules must respect Linha's retention period.

docs.title: Maintain the documentation
docs.text: The site uses pinned MkDocs, Material and mike versions. Markdown stays in docs/; GitHub Pages serves development docs and frozen snapshots from new release tags. This guide is for contributors and maintainers.

docs.title: Preview and validate locally
docs.text:
python3 -m venv /tmp/linha-docs-env
/tmp/linha-docs-env/bin/python -m pip install -r docs/requirements.txt
/tmp/linha-docs-env/bin/mkdocs serve

Open the local URL printed by MkDocs. For a strict build and versioning check:

PATH=/tmp/linha-docs-env/bin:$PATH mkdocs build --strict
PATH=/tmp/linha-docs-env/bin:$PATH python3 scripts/check-docs.py
python3 scripts/check-public-content.py

The versioning check uses a temporary Git repository. It verifies release snapshot preservation, development updates, version metadata, root redirects and rejection of attempts to replace a release snapshot with a different source commit. It does not write to GitHub or alter branches in your checkout.

Generated site/ output is ignored. Local validation logs and JSON evidence are excluded from the site even when they exist under docs/validation/.

docs.title: Audit public content
docs.text:
CI runs the generic workspace-path check and its synthetic fixture tests. It does not contain organization-specific names, identifier hashes or a private denylist. Fork pull requests run the same generic checks without receiving private policy.

Maintainers can perform an additional local-only identifier audit. Supply LINHA_PUBLIC_CONTENT_DENYLIST as a JSON array of identifiers. For example, a policy for an invented integration could contain:

["internal-workload", "corp.example", "io.example"]

Keep the real policy outside the checkout and generated site. Load it from a private local file and require it before inspecting source, history or output:

export LINHA_PUBLIC_CONTENT_DENYLIST="$(cat /tmp/linha-private-denylist.json)"
python3 scripts/check-public-content.py --require-denylist
python3 scripts/check-public-content.py --history --require-denylist
python3 scripts/check-public-content.py --directory site --require-denylist
unset LINHA_PUBLIC_CONTENT_DENYLIST

--require-denylist fails when the policy is absent, empty or invalid. Omitting it permits the generic path check when no policy is configured; a supplied malformed policy still fails. Identifier matching is case-insensitive and checks whole names, separator components, domain suffixes and adjacent dotted pairs, including package prefixes within longer class names. Diagnostics report only file/line locations and never matched source text or policy values.

Do not commit the policy, embed hashes of its values or send it to CI. The local identifier audit complements the generic CI check; CI success does not establish that an organization-specific audit has run.

docs.title: Choose one page purpose
docs.text:
Reader need Page type Writing pattern Learn through a working example Tutorial State prerequisites, give numbered steps and verify each outcome Complete a known task How-to guide State assumptions, give focused actions and expected results Look up a field or contract Reference Use consistent names, types, defaults and bounds Understand a design choice Explanation Describe concepts, lifetime and trade-offs; link to procedures

This follows Diátaxis. Cross-link related types rather than mixing long explanations into a copyable task. Examples use reserved .example hostnames and invented workloads. Public docs must not contain real integration project names, corporate deployment identifiers, secrets or personal workspace paths.

docs.title: Publish on GitHub Pages
docs.text:
The documentation workflow validates every pull request. A main-branch push updates dev; a new vX.Y.Z tag captures version X.Y.Z. The greatest stable release version owns latest; publishing an older backport leaves that alias unchanged. Prereleases move prerelease. The root redirects to latest when it exists, otherwise to dev or the first version.

The workflow preserves generated snapshots on docs-pages, uploads the complete site as a Pages artifact and deploys it through the github-pages environment. Source branches and release tags are not rewritten by documentation publication. Previously published HTML is retained rather than rebuilt using newer tooling. The version selector reads versions.json generated by mike. Release builds render their SDK/image versions and omit development-only notices; the source Markdown keeps copyable examples for the current development checkout. Historical release notes retain their original version fields.

The workflow requests contents: write only to preserve snapshots, pages: write for the deployment and id-token: write for its Pages identity. Pull-request checks have read-only repository permissions. Configure GitHub Pages to use GitHub Actions; the workflow can enable Pages when the repository's settings permit it. Environment branch/tag restrictions must permit the intended main branch and tags.

The first site publication does not rebuild older tags into versioned snapshots. Their release notes remain available, and future tags capture their own docs. A repeated publication of the same source/version reuses its frozen HTML. A version already associated with a different source commit is rejected.

See mike, Material versioning and GitHub Pages workflows for the hosting mechanics. The build intentionally pins MkDocs 1.6.1 and the compatible plugin/theme versions; upgrades require a strict build and snapshot test.

docs.title: HTTP API reference
docs.text: The base protocol is JSON over HTTP. Typed SDK calls wrap the same envelopes. The full OpenAPI document contains request/response schemas and bounds; these tables are a lookup guide.

docs.title: Public routes
docs.text:
Authenticated requests use Authorization: Bearer <access-token>. Ownership is derived from that token, never from caller-supplied JSON.

Method / route Purpose POST /v1/contexts:ensure Derive a backend version and acquire a client lease GET /v1/contexts/{context} Context status POST /v1/contexts/{context}/clients Attach to a persisted version POST /v1/contexts/{context}/clients/{lease}/renew Renew a live lease DELETE /v1/contexts/{context}/clients/{lease} Release a lease idempotently POST /v1/contexts/{context}/jobs Persist a new job; requires X-Linha-Client-Lease GET /v1/jobs Owner-scoped job list with bounded pagination GET /v1/jobs/{job} Status, progress and final failure GET /v1/jobs/{job}/attempts Persisted attempts POST /v1/jobs/{job}:cancel Request cancellation GET /v1/jobs/{job}/result Published result metadata GET /v1/jobs/{job}/files/{output} Stream an authorized file GET /v1/jobs/{job}/parts Paginated dataset part metadata GET /v1/jobs/{job}/part?path=... Stream an authorized dataset part

Ensure accepts name, clientId, optional hostname and spec; the response includes id, version and clientLease. Polling does not renew a lease.

A job envelope is:

{
  "handler": "count-rows",
  "version": 1,
  "payload": {"size": 1000},
  "idempotencyKey": "request-42",
  "retry": {"maxAttempts": 1, "backoffSeconds": 1}
}

A raw worker registers the same handler/version and maps the payload to business code. Duplicate capability registration is rejected. Classes and executable closures do not travel through this envelope.

docs.title: State and errors
docs.text:
Job states are QUEUED, RETRYING, RUNNING, CANCELLING, SUCCEEDED, FAILED and CANCELLED. Retrying work can be in backoff. Final result retrieval requires successful publication and an unexpired retained payload.

Errors use this envelope:

{"error":{"code":"FORBIDDEN","message":"administrator role required"}}
Code / condition Meaning UNAUTHORIZED Missing or invalid credentials FORBIDDEN Valid identity lacks the required admin action CLIENT_LEASE_EXPIRED Attach again to acquire a new context lease Idempotency conflict Same owner/name/key with different request or policy SCHEMA_MISMATCH Typed result descriptor differs from the retained descriptor RESULT_EXPIRED Payload retention ended; status metadata remains DESTINATION_CHANGED Stored destination identity no longer matches configuration DATASET_UNSUPPORTED Destination cannot safely delegate a distributed write STAGING_LIMIT_EXCEEDED Concurrent staging reservation budget exhausted

Foreign job identifiers are not a way to access another owner's history. See failure diagnosis for exceptions and traces.

docs.title: Worker and administrator routes
docs.text:
Worker registration, heartbeat, claim, renew, output allocation/upload, part registration/sealing, completion and failure routes use managed worker identity plus current-attempt fencing. They are runtime protocol operations, not application OAuth requests.

/v1/admin/* is a separate cross-owner inspection/action surface. It requires viewer/operator membership from the browser issuer. Mutations require operator access; cookie mutations also require origin/CSRF checks. The console guide covers setup.

docs.title: Batch request actions
docs.text:
POST /v1/admin/jobs/batch requires operator access. Browser requests also send same-origin Origin and X-Linha-CSRF headers. Supply 1–200 unique requests and the context version each selection came from:

{
  "action": "move",
  "targetContextId": "corrected-context-id",
  "jobs": [
    {"id": "request-id", "contextId": "old-context-id"}
  ]
}

Use action: "cancel" and omit targetContextId for cancellation. A malformed batch returns a structured HTTP error before any item changes. A valid batch returns HTTP 200 with items; inspect each item's outcome and optional error. An eligible item returns its unchanged public id and a compact job summary (context, state, attempt count and update time); payloads are not duplicated in batch responses. Failed items contain a safe code and message and do not roll back other items.

Moves preserve original requests, result policies and retry history. They require an active destination of the same owner, logical name and engine type/version, with unchanged source workload-storage access. Audit records for moves include sourceContextId and destination contextId. See queue recovery for the operator procedure.

docs.title: Operational routes
docs.text:
Route Response purpose /livez Process liveness /readyz Database/schema and configured local storage readiness /metrics Prometheus exposition when enabled /ui/ Administrator console when enabled

There is no /health Prometheus route. Scrapes do not acquire context leases.

docs.title: Diagnose failed jobs and authentication
docs.text: Use the saved job ID to inspect status and every persisted attempt. These records survive server and worker restarts. A final job summary may differ from an earlier failed attempt when retries or deadlines are involved.

docs.title: Inspect the failure
docs.text:
Fetch GET /v1/jobs/{job} and GET /v1/jobs/{job}/attempts, or call handle.status() and handle.attempts(). An illustrative JVM failure is:

{
  "code": "OUT_OF_MEMORY",
  "message": "Java heap space",
  "retryable": false,
  "exceptionType": "java.lang.OutOfMemoryError",
  "phase": "handler",
  "stackTrace": "java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space\n\tat example.ReportJob.execute(ReportJob.scala:42)\n...",
  "stackTraceTruncated": false
}

exceptionType is the caught exception. The trace includes ordinary Caused by and Suppressed sections; a Spark wrapper retains its underlying cause chain. Phases are initialization, engine, handler, result and completion. The code OUT_OF_MEMORY is based on an observed error type, not message matching.

docs.title: Find the worker evidence
docs.text:
Search worker logs by job ID. Error headers include job, attempt, worker, handler/version and phase; the full exception follows. Failure-reporting and cleanup errors are correlated separately and do not replace the original failure.

If a Pod was killed, inspect its termination state and executor logs. Kubernetes OOM kills and JVM crashes may prevent any trace from being sent. The attempt still follows lease-loss recovery. Verify JVM heap plus overhead in Spark resource settings rather than setting container memory equal to the heap.

docs.title: Decide whether to retry
docs.text: Execution retries default to one total attempt. Set maxAttempts when submitting only if repeating the business operation is safe. A driver replacement does not by itself opt a request into retry. Cancellation takes precedence when its intent is committed before completion. Idempotency protects duplicate acceptance, not all external business effects.

docs.title: Diagnose OAuth and access failures
docs.text:
Symptom Check SDK credential acquisition fails Exact token endpoint, client authentication/service account enabled, current client secret 401 from Linha JWT signature, issuer, audience linha, expiry and nonempty subject 403 on admin routes Browser group/role claim and security.admin rules; API service credentials do not grant admin TLS failure Provider CA trust for the SDK and server independently Status/result disappears after identity change Same issuer and subject as the original owner

The OAuth SDK reports operation/status without provider bodies or credentials. Keep the original cause in application logs only when it is already sanitized; do not log tokens, client secrets or full system-property dumps.

docs.title: Diagnostic limits
docs.text: The wire bounds messages to 8192 UTF-8 bytes, exception types to 1024 and stack traces to 65536. The JVM captures at most 16384 UTF-16 code units and marks truncation. Full traces remain in worker stderr when available. Older stored failures without diagnostic fields cannot be reconstructed retroactively.

docs.title: Run disposable Kubernetes validation
docs.text: The cluster scripts exercise managed Spark, replicas, resources and retained results. They are development fixtures, not a way to test an existing installation. Use only their named disposable clusters and databases.

docs.title: Prepare the fixture inputs
docs.text:
Install Docker, Kind, Helm, kubectl, Java 17, Python 3 and the normal project build requirements. The recorded Kind baseline is Kubernetes 1.33.1 with about eight available CPUs and 32 GiB memory.

Build the server and connector-equipped worker:

make build
scripts/prepare-spark-connectors.sh
mvn -B package
docker build -f server/Dockerfile -t linha/server:platform-complete .
docker build -f examples/spark/Dockerfile -t linha/spark-example:platform-complete .

The current platform fixture also requires a compatible MinIO server image tagged linha/minio:validation-glibc. Provide that local fixture image before starting; it is a test input, not a published Linha artifact.

The scripts read Spark Operator's chart from a fixed temporary checkout:

git clone --branch v2.4.0 --depth 1   https://github.com/kubeflow/spark-operator.git /tmp/linha-spark-operator-v2.4.0

Do not replace a pre-existing temporary checkout without checking its purpose.

docs.title: Run the current platform sequence
docs.text:
python3 scripts/platform-fixtures.py start
python3 scripts/platform-results-e2e.py
python3 scripts/platform-fault-e2e.py
python3 scripts/platform-cluster-e2e.py
python3 scripts/platform-load-e2e.py
python3 scripts/platform-final-smoke.py
python3 scripts/platform-fixtures.py clean

Run sequentially: fault checks pause their fixture database. The cluster script creates a dedicated linha-platform-* Kind cluster and kubeconfig, loads images, and installs the operator. Its state is recorded in /tmp/linha-platform-cluster-state.json; the local fixture state is /tmp/linha-release-fixtures.json.

Capture needed evidence before clean. Cleanup removes only labelled fixture containers and the cluster described by its validated state. Locally built images remain. If a run stops early, inspect that fixture's state and logs before cleanup.

docs.title: Use the focused template fixture
docs.text:
scripts/pod-template-e2e.py --state <state-file> expects an already prepared linha-pods-* Kind cluster, matching dedicated context/kubeconfig, loaded worker image and disposable PostgreSQL container. It checks driver/executor templates, resources, allocation, replacement and retained results. Read the script's state validation before supplying a state file.

The older cluster-e2e.py and restart-e2e.py record earlier launch paths and require their own preinstalled fixture. Prefer the current platform/template sequence for SparkApplication and client-lease behavior.

A single Kind host and shared POSIX volume establish application recovery only. See validation scope for the limits of these checks.

docs.title: Prometheus metric reference
docs.text: These families are exported from /metrics. They supplement the older compatibility aliases retained by the server. Every family has HELP and TYPE metadata. Seconds and bytes are base units. Histogram names imply _bucket{le}, _sum, and _count; Info is a gauge with value 1.

docs.title: Scope and labels
docs.text:
Shared metrics describe durable database state. Every server exposes the same values, so deduplicate replicas before aggregation. Local metrics describe one process; retain Pod identity or sum per-Pod rates. Observed metrics describe persisted current engine observations; deduplicate and require complete, fresh data.

Labels engine,context identify the bounded persisted context registry. Storage labels provider,destination identify the provider and configured destination alias, never a bucket URI. Scrape discovery supplies deployment labels such as cluster, namespace, linha_deployment, pod and instance.

Tables use C for engine,context and D for provider,destination to keep individual entries compact. No request ID, owner, exception text or result path is a metric label. Failed snapshots omit shared series; a known zero is emitted only from a successful snapshot. See HA query examples.

docs.title: Clients and contexts
docs.text:
Name Type/scope Labels Meaning linha_client_leases Gauge Shared C, state Current stored lease generations: active, expired, released; active uses database-clock expiry. linha_client_lease_events_total Counter Shared C, event Acquired, explicitly released, or expired generations, once per event/generation. Renewals do not count as acquisitions. linha_context_versions Gauge Shared C, state Immutable versions in each normalized lifecycle state. linha_context_versions_with_demand Gauge Shared C, demand Versions with live clients or accepted work, reported separately as clients|work; one version can have both, so do not sum these as distinct versions. linha_context_conditions Gauge Shared C, reason Versions with a provisioning/lifecycle condition, grouped by fixed platform reason. linha_metrics_context_labels Gauge Shared state Number of permanently assigned named dimensions and logical contexts grouped into overflow.

Expired/released lease rows are record counts, not current demand; historical acquisition/release/expiry rates use counters. Client identifiers and exact last-seen times are available in the admin API only.

docs.title: Jobs and execution
docs.text:
Name Type/scope Labels Meaning linha_job_records Gauge Shared C, state Retained jobs currently in QUEUED, RETRYING, RUNNING, CANCELLING, SUCCEEDED, FAILED, CANCELLED; terminal values include retained history. linha_queue_jobs Gauge Shared C, eligibility Queued/retrying work classified ready|backoff; never includes running work. linha_queue_oldest_age_seconds Gauge Shared C Age since original submission of oldest QUEUED/RETRYING job, including retry backoff; zero for an empty queue. linha_job_submissions_total Counter Shared C, source Newly committed jobs (sdk|admin), excluding idempotent repeats. linha_job_completions_total Counter Shared C, outcome First committed terminal job transitions: SUCCEEDED, FAILED, CANCELLED. linha_job_failures_total Counter Shared C, reason Terminal FAILED jobs classified by bounded reason; business exception text never becomes a label. linha_job_retries_total Counter Shared C, reason Persisted additional-attempt decisions, not duplicate claim attempts. linha_attempts_current Gauge Shared C, state Nonterminal current attempts with running|cancelling|lease_expired, a disjoint classification. linha_attempt_completions_total Counter Shared C, outcome First persisted attempt termination, including failure/interruption/cancellation; duplicate completion callbacks excluded. linha_job_queue_wait_seconds Histogram Shared C Submission to first assignment, exactly one observation when first claimed. linha_attempt_duration_seconds Histogram Shared C Assignment to persisted terminal attempt state, exactly one observation per terminated attempt. linha_job_duration_seconds Histogram Shared C, outcome Submission to terminal job outcome, including retries and queue wait. linha_job_cancellation_duration_seconds Histogram Shared C First cancellation intent to CANCELLED; success-before-cancel is excluded. linha_worker_updates_rejected_total Counter Local operation,reason Rejected worker reports; operations are a fixed set and reasons include identity mismatch, stale attempt, expired lease, invalid state, invalid payload, and other. linha_accounting_started_timestamp_seconds Gauge Shared none Baseline of new durable lifecycle counters/histograms; old history is represented by gauges, not fabricated events.

Fixed failure categories: business_error, lease_expired, worker_lost, deadline_exceeded, provisioning, result_storage, invalid_result, other. Map arbitrary worker failure codes into this set. Do not label by handler or exception type. Attempts use documented normalized outcomes SUCCEEDED|FAILED|CANCELLED|INTERRUPTED; preserve richer raw states in the detail API.

Job/attempt/queue/cancellation histogram boundaries: 0.1, 1, 5, 15, 30, 60, 120, 300, 600, 1800, 3600, 10800, 43200, 86400 seconds, plus +Inf. Bucket changes are a metric contract change, not an arbitrary per-replica setting.

docs.title: Workers and engines
docs.text:
Name Type/scope Labels Meaning linha_workers Gauge Shared C, state Registered workers classified ready|draining|stale; stale takes precedence over draining. linha_worker_capacity_slots Gauge Shared C Total configured claim slots on fresh non-draining registered workers. linha_worker_occupied_slots Gauge Shared C Slots held by unexpired current running/cancelling attempts on those workers; unrelated/stale instances are excluded. linha_engine_instances Gauge Shared C, state Managed instances by lifecycle state, including STARTING, READY, DRAINING, DEAD. linha_engine_desired_instances Gauge Shared C Current desired instance count after client/work lifetime and scaler rules, not just configured minimum. linha_engine_configured_instances Gauge Shared C, bound Sum of configured min|max for versions with current demand; stopped versions do not inflate limits. linha_engine_provisioning_duration_seconds Histogram Shared C Instance demand to first ready registered worker, boundaries 1, 5, 15, 30, 60, 120, 300, 600, 1800, +Inf. linha_engine_instances_replaced_total Counter Shared C, reason Persisted replacement decisions for lost/failed instances; reconciliation polls are not new events. linha_engine_observations Gauge Shared C, state Required live-instance observations classified fresh|stale|missing, measured independently of their content. linha_engine_observation_oldest_timestamp_seconds Gauge Shared C Oldest observation among currently required observed instances; missing observations are indicated separately. linha_spark_driver_pods Gauge Observed C, state Current owned Spark driver pods by normalized Kubernetes phase, separate from SDK readiness. linha_spark_executor_pods Gauge Observed C, state Current owned executor pods by phase; deleted executors disappear. linha_spark_executor_configuration Gauge Shared C, bound Sum of configured executor min|initial|max across currently desired drivers; static instances use the same value for all three. linha_spark_pod_cpu_cores Gauge Observed C, role,allocation Sum of Spark main-container CPU requests/limits; role driver/executor, allocation request/limit. linha_spark_pod_memory_bytes Gauge Observed C, role,allocation Sum of observed Spark main-container memory requests/limits, including container overhead; not memory usage.

Normalize pod phases to Pending|Running|Succeeded|Failed|Unknown|Terminating, using Terminating when deletion is observed. Ready workers and Running pods are not interchangeable. Desired demand can change between snapshots; explicitly timestamp it. Do not publish partial resource totals as complete when a quantity is missing; expose a fixed missing_resources observation condition in the internal detail/condition projection.

docs.title: Servers, dependencies, and background loops
docs.text:
Name Type/scope Labels Meaning linha_server_build_info Info Local version,revision Build metadata, once per responding server. linha_server_ready Gauge Local none Latest bounded readiness observation, 0/1; timestamped by its collector. linha_servers Gauge Shared state Latest process per server pod classified ready|unready|stale|stopping, with 24-hour heartbeat retention. linha_dependency_available Gauge Local dependency Latest configured database/local-storage check; 0/1, never fabricated for an unchecked service. linha_background_loop_runs_total Counter Local loop,outcome Runs of reconcile/recovery/retention/cleanup/heartbeat/observation, success/error. linha_background_loop_duration_seconds Histogram Local loop Duration of each loop run, including errors. linha_background_loop_last_success_timestamp_seconds Gauge Local loop Last success; zero before the first success. linha_database_pool_connections Gauge Local state Acquired, idle, constructing connections. linha_database_pool_max_connections Gauge Local none Configured pool capacity. linha_database_pool_acquire_wait_seconds_total Counter Local none Accumulated pool acquisition wait time. linha_database_pool_acquire_failures_total Counter Local reason Timeout/cancel/error acquisition failures. linha_kubernetes_api_requests_total Counter Local resource,verb,outcome Bounded resource/verb set and outcome success/forbidden/not_found/timeout/error. linha_kubernetes_api_duration_seconds Histogram Local resource,verb Kubernetes call latency without names, selectors, URLs, or error strings. linha_collector_success Gauge Local collector Latest collection completed successfully, 0/1. linha_collector_last_success_timestamp_seconds Gauge Local collector Last usable sample time; zero before initialization. linha_collector_duration_seconds Histogram Local collector Background collection latency. linha_collector_errors_total Counter Local collector,reason Bounded timeout/unavailable/invalid/other errors.

Use fixed collector names database|readiness|engine_snapshot; the engine_snapshot collector reports completeness of required engine observations, while per-context detail identifies gaps. No synthetic up metric: Prometheus supplies up per scrape target. Standard Go/process collectors supply CPU time, resident memory, goroutines, GC and process start time. Runtime metrics do not imply Kubernetes pod readiness; optional external dashboards can use kube-state-metrics for desired replica count and pod restarts.

docs.title: HTTP and results/storage
docs.text:
Name Type/scope Labels Meaning linha_api_requests_total Counter Local route,method,status_code All API responses, including unauthorized, worker and admin routes, and unmatched paths; probes, metrics and static assets are excluded. linha_api_request_duration_seconds Histogram Local route,method Time through response completion, including streamed results. linha_api_requests_in_flight Gauge Local route,method Currently executing API requests. linha_api_response_bytes_total Counter Local route,method Bytes written by API responses. linha_results Gauge Shared C, D, state Published result sets classified retained/expired, not per-file parts. linha_result_published_bytes Gauge Shared C, D, state Logical published file/part bytes recorded in manifests; exclude manifest bytes from dataset part totals and do not count replicas/staging copies. linha_result_cleanup_candidates Gauge Shared D Allocations currently eligible under terminal/expiry/delegation/grace rules. linha_result_cleanup_runs_total Counter Local D, outcome Cleanup executions success/error; these are operations, not exactly-once object deletion counts. linha_storage_operations_total Counter Local D, operation,outcome Server-observed allocate/upload/download/publish/list/delete/delegate/probe/other operations. linha_storage_operation_duration_seconds Histogram Local D, operation Complete server-observed operation latency. linha_storage_transferred_bytes_total Counter Local D, direction Server-observed upload/download bytes; direct worker/Spark S3 writes are excluded. linha_staging_reserved_bytes Gauge Local none Current server staging budget reservation. linha_staging_limit_bytes Gauge Local none Configured server staging reservation limit.

HTTP/local operation duration boundaries: 0.005, 0.01, 0.025, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2.5, 5, 10, 30, 60, +Inf. Storage/JVM business failures also appear in durable job failure categories when they terminate a request; local storage call metrics do not claim to cover direct worker I/O.

docs.title: Compatibility and validation
docs.text: The old unlabeled HTTP counters and legacy shared gauges retain their original name/shape for one release. New code registers no mixed-definition family. Tests parse exposition, assert HELP/TYPE, escaped values and zero states, and verify fixture totals against PostgreSQL. Test HTTP route normalization with attacker-chosen paths/methods and label-registry overflow with more than the configured context budget. Report the measured series count and SQL/collection cost in validation documentation.

docs.title: Monitor queries and resources
docs.text: Use Prometheus for trends and Grafana for the operational dashboard. Use the administrator console for exact requests, exceptions and instance details. Linha exports /metrics; /livez and /readyz are separate probes.

docs.title: 1. Enable per-replica scraping
docs.text:
The metrics route is enabled by default. With Prometheus Operator installed:

metrics:
  enabled: true
  cluster: production
  serviceMonitor:
    enabled: true
    labels:
      release: kube-prometheus-stack
    interval: 30s
    scrapeTimeout: 10s
    sampleLimit: 100000

Set labels that match your Prometheus ServiceMonitor selector. The resource selects the release Service's named HTTP port and discovers each server Pod independently. It adds no Linha ClusterRole. Keep scrape access inside your operational network; the metrics route does not use application OAuth or admin sessions.

Without the operator, configure Prometheus to scrape each Pod rather than one load-balanced Service address. Cluster, namespace, deployment and Pod labels come from scrape discovery.

docs.title: 2. Install the dashboard
docs.text:
Import the dashboard JSON into Grafana and choose its Prometheus datasource. Alternatively, with Grafana Operator installed:

metrics:
  grafanaDashboard:
    enabled: true
    instanceSelector:
      matchLabels:
        dashboards: platform
    folder: Linha
    datasourceUID: prometheus
    allowCrossNamespaceImport: false

ServiceMonitor and GrafanaDashboard are independently optional. Enabling either requires its installed CRD. For offline Helm rendering, pass the corresponding --api-versions flag. Set ui.grafanaURL to link from the console.

docs.title: 3. Read the dashboard
docs.text:
Question Relevant panels Is work moving? Running, queued, succeeded and failed queries; completion rate and success rate Where is time spent? Queue wait, attempt processing, end-to-end duration and oldest queued request Do we have capacity? Connected clients, active versions, ready workers and occupied/available slots What resources are allocated? Running drivers/executors; CPU and memory requests/limits Are measurements trustworthy? Ready servers, collector age, API/dependency failures and observation completeness

Filter by cluster, namespace, deployment, engine and context. Completed outcomes refer to the selected time range, not the lifetime count of retained job records. Success rate excludes cancellation. Processing time measures completed attempts; retries count separately. End-to-end time includes queueing and retries.

CPU/memory panels show allocations, not live usage. Use your existing container metrics source for usage. Retired instances are excluded; missing or stale engine observations make the total unavailable rather than showing a partial healthy sum.

docs.title: 4. Write correct HA queries
docs.text:
All server replicas export the same durable business state. Deduplicate those copies before summing or taking rates. Local HTTP/runtime counters belong to each process; calculate each process rate and then sum.

Running requests across the selected deployment:

sum(max by (cluster, namespace, linha_deployment, engine, context, state) (
  linha_job_records{state="RUNNING"}
))

Ready and backoff work in the queue:

sum by (eligibility) (
  max by (cluster, namespace, linha_deployment, engine, context, eligibility) (
    linha_queue_jobs
  )
)

Failed jobs over five minutes:

sum(increase((
  max by (cluster, namespace, linha_deployment, engine, context, outcome) (
    linha_job_completions_total{outcome="FAILED"}
  )
)[5m:15s]))

p95 processing duration of completed attempts:

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate((
  max by (cluster, namespace, linha_deployment, engine, context, le) (
    linha_attempt_duration_seconds_bucket
  )
)[5m:15s])))

Local API error rate:

sum(rate(linha_api_requests_total{status_code=~"5.."}[5m]))

Apply the same deployment filters to every expression when several deployments share Prometheus. Shared histogram deduplication must include le. The complete metric reference identifies each family's scope and labels.

docs.title: Diagnose missing data or excess API traffic
docs.text:
Database snapshots refresh every ten seconds with a two-second timeout. Scrapes read a cache and do not call PostgreSQL, Kubernetes or storage. A failed collection omits shared families and still returns local metrics with HTTP 200; it does not pretend the queue is empty. Check collector success and last-success timestamps.

Context labels are lifetime-bounded: the first metrics.maxContexts owner/name dimensions get stable labels, and further names aggregate as __other__. No job ID, exception text, owner, result URI or version hash becomes a metric label.

Active capacity reconciles frequently. Retired engine resources are inventoried once per minute per replica, independent of dead history size. In an empty namespace this costs three collection requests per minute per replica. Repeated individual GET/DELETE 404s from an idle deployment can indicate an older replica still running. Inspect the process-local linha_kubernetes_api_requests_total rate by resource, verb and outcome.

Engine cleanup is automatic; result-file cleanup is a separate opt-in setting. See result retention and validation.

docs.title: Deploy Linha on Kubernetes
docs.text: This guide installs an HA API service with managed Spark backends. It assumes you already operate Kubernetes, Helm, PostgreSQL and either S3 or a shared persistent filesystem.

docs.title: 1. Prepare the dependencies
docs.text:
Create a namespace for Linha and its workers. Install Kubeflow Spark Operator 2.4.0 separately, with sparkoperator.k8s.io/v1beta2 SparkApplication support and the operator watching this namespace. Linha's chart does not install the operator or its CRDs. Namespace-only Linha RBAC does not change the operator's own permissions.

Provision a durable PostgreSQL service and result storage. All server replicas must use the same database. For local results, every server, driver and executor must see the same persistent filesystem at the configured root.

docs.title: 2. Create database and storage Secrets
docs.text:
Provide a Secret in the release namespace with separate username and password keys. Set its name through database.postgres.secretRef. Credentials are URI-encoded by the server; do not manually escape characters in the Secret values.

For S3, provide a Secret key containing destination JSON:

{
  "analytics": {
    "bucket": "example-results",
    "prefix": "linha",
    "region": "eu-west-1"
  }
}

Optional endpoint and pathStyle: true support S3-compatible stores. Server credentials use the AWS default credential chain. Callers select a destination alias and path policy; storage credentials do not travel in job JSON.

docs.title: 3. Select a matching image
docs.text:
Use the server image matching your chart and documentation version.

The example below selects a source-built image. For a published release, select ghcr.io/k3rnl/linha/server and its matching release tag instead.

docs.title: 4. Create a values file
docs.text:
replicaCount: 2
image:
  repository: registry.example/linha/server
  tag: development
database:
  postgres:
    host: postgres.example.internal
    database: linha
    sslMode: verify-full
    secretRef: linha-postgres
    usernameKey: username
    passwordKey: password
security:
  enabled: true
  api:
    enabled: true
    jwt:
      issuer: https://identity.example/realms/jobs
      audience: linha
  oidc:
    enabled: false
rbac:
  namespaceOnly: true
allowedImages:
  - registry.example/workers
s3:
  enabled: true
  secretRef: linha-results
  destinationsKey: destinations

allowedImages must include each permitted worker repository prefix. Use a broad allow-list only when all callers and images share the deployment's trust boundary. Configure private registry Secret references through Pod templates.

The chart derives the internal worker server URL from its Service. Applications use the Service address or a separately exposed API route. The UI ingress exposes only UI/admin routes and is not a public job API ingress.

docs.title: 5. Install and verify
docs.text:
From the source checkout:

helm upgrade --install linha deploy/helm/linha   --namespace linha --create-namespace --values values.yaml
kubectl -n linha rollout status deployment/linha-linha
kubectl -n linha get pods
kubectl -n linha port-forward service/linha-linha 8080:8080

In another terminal, check readiness:

curl --fail http://localhost:8080/readyz

Readiness checks PostgreSQL and configured local storage. Liveness checks the process. Inspect server logs if readiness or startup fails.

docs.title: 6. Configure clients and Spark
docs.text:
Use OAuth client credentials for application clients. Ensure a backend with your worker image and Spark application settings. Put handler code, matching SDKs and any required connectors in that image.

Add the administrator console and Prometheus/Grafana integration when needed.

docs.title: Private certificates
docs.text:
For PostgreSQL, mount its CA and set database.postgres.sslRootCert. For the identity provider, mount a CA directory and extend the system trust path:

extraEnv:
  - name: SSL_CERT_DIR
    value: /etc/ssl/certs:/etc/linha/identity-ca
extraVolumes:
  - name: identity-ca
    configMap:
      name: linha-identity-ca
extraVolumeMounts:
  - name: identity-ca
    mountPath: /etc/linha/identity-ca
    readOnly: true

The ConfigMap must contain PEM certificate files. Roll the server after changing its CA files. Keep /etc/ssl/certs in the path to retain public roots.

The explicit security.api.jwt.tls.insecureSkipVerify and security.oidc.tls.insecureSkipVerify switches bypass provider certificate and hostname verification independently. They retain JWT checks but permit provider impersonation; trusting the CA preserves the full verification boundary. Browser certificate trust is independent of these server options.

docs.title: Namespace-only worker permissions
docs.text:
