The default rbac.namespaceOnly: true creates Roles and RoleBindings, with no ClusterRole. Workers authenticate through Kubernetes issuer discovery and signing keys plus live Pod/service-account checks. A cluster that removed the default service-account discovery access must restore it or choose rbac.namespaceOnly: false to use TokenReview. Resource management stays in the release namespace in both cases.

Spark cleanup needs deletecollection on Pods and ConfigMaps. Verify the worker Role if Spark reports a collection-delete permission error:

kubectl -n linha auth can-i deletecollection pods   --as=system:serviceaccount:linha:linha-linha-worker
kubectl -n linha auth can-i deletecollection configmaps   --as=system:serviceaccount:linha:linha-linha-worker

Both should return yes; the caller needs permission to impersonate the account.

docs.title: Upgrade and recover
docs.text:
Back up PostgreSQL before an upgrade. Deploy a matching server, chart and SDK set when configuration or protocol changes require it. Database migrations are serialized. Older binaries can reject a newer schema; do not start an older binary against it without a compatible rollback procedure.

Retain the same result destination locations when upgrading. Changing a bucket, prefix or endpoint under an existing destination alias can invalidate its stored fingerprint; use a new alias for a new location. Credentials can rotate separately.

Process restarts preserve metadata, but recovery still depends on the durability of PostgreSQL and result storage. See architecture and validation scope for the tested boundaries.

docs.title: Customize driver and executor Pods
docs.text:
Pass native Kubernetes fragments through engine.settings.kubernetes.driverPodTemplate and executorPodTemplate when ensuring a backend. Use this for configuration files, Secret references, private registry pulls, scheduling, sidecars and init containers.

Resources you reference must already exist in the Linha namespace. Templates contain metadata labels/annotations and spec; omit Pod names, namespaces, apiVersion and kind.

docs.title: Add files, environment and pull Secrets
docs.text:
import linha.client._
import io.circe.Json
import io.circe.syntax._

val shared = PodTemplate.empty
  .withConfigMap("app-config", "reporting-config-v1", "/etc/reporting")
  .withSecretEnv("APP_PASSWORD", "reporting-credentials", "password")
  .withImagePullSecret("worker-registry")

val templates = SparkPodTemplates(
  driver = shared.withEnv("APP_ROLE", "driver"),
  executor = shared.withEnv("APP_ROLE", "executor")
)
val settings = templates.withSettings(Json.obj(
  "application" -> Json.obj(
    "mainClass" -> "example.WorkerMain".asJson,
    "mainApplicationFile" -> "local:///opt/linha/worker.jar".asJson
  ),
  "drivers" -> Json.obj("minDrivers" -> 1.asJson, "maxDrivers" -> 2.asJson),
  "executors" -> Json.obj("instances" -> 2.asJson)
))

Put settings inside the Spark engine spec. Driver and executor templates are independent; apply shared values to both when Spark tasks need them. Helpers also support Secret/PVC volumes, JSON, YAML and files. YAML is parsed locally and sent as JSON; file paths and callbacks are not transmitted.

The raw JSON equivalent belongs under engine.settings:

{
  "kubernetes": {
    "driverPodTemplate": {
      "spec": {
        "imagePullSecrets": [{"name": "worker-registry"}],
        "volumes": [{"name": "app-config", "configMap": {"name": "reporting-config-v1"}}],
        "containers": [{
          "name": "main",
          "volumeMounts": [{"name": "app-config", "mountPath": "/etc/reporting", "readOnly": true}]
        }]
      }
    }
  }
}

Use main for the Spark main container in public templates. Linha translates it to the driver/executor names used by Spark.

docs.title: Permit private registry Secrets
docs.text:
registrySecrets:
  allowedNames: [worker-registry]
workerPodTemplates:
  driverPodTemplate:
    spec:
      nodeSelector: {workload: spark}
  executorPodTemplate:
    spec:
      nodeSelector: {workload: spark}

Create the selected registry Secret as kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson or kubernetes.io/dockercfg. The server Role permits get only on approved registry Secret names for image digest resolution. The names, not credential values, enter the persisted spec. Kubelet uses the same Secret for pulling.

Top-level imagePullSecrets also apply to the server and become worker defaults; those names are automatically permitted. registrySecrets.allowedNames only permits selection and does not attach the Secret. Use explicit registry/repository auth keys; wildcard keys are not supported by Linha's resolver.

docs.title: Understand merge and protected fields
docs.text:
Deployment defaults are merged first, then the client template. Objects merge recursively. Containers, init containers, env, volumes and image pull Secrets merge by name; mounts merge by mountPath. Other arrays replace. Empty named arrays preserve inherited entries. Null/delete/JSON-patch directives are unsupported.

The normalized effective template is saved with the context version. Changing Helm defaults affects future ensures; existing versions and replacements keep their saved template. Use versioned immutable ConfigMaps/Secrets for reproducibility.

Linha reserves Pod identity, service accounts, ownership labels, worker token mounts, restart policy and the main image/command/args/working directory. LINHA_* and SPARK_* env names and runtime mount paths are protected. Set main CPU and memory through Spark settings, not the container template. Sidecars and init images follow the image allow-list too.

Each template is limited to 64 KiB, including after merging. Conflicting managed fields return a validation error. Kubernetes admission and scheduling errors remain visible through context conditions.

docs.title: Protocol identity and conformance
docs.text: The request identity is a handler name, positive handler version and JSON payload. Typed codecs serialize parameters into that envelope. Workers execute only registered classes already installed in the image.

docs.title: Context version encoding
docs.text:
The server normalizes defaults, resources, durations, result destination identity, merged Pod templates and the resolved main-image digest. It recursively sorts JSON object keys, preserves array order, encodes with Go JSON escaping and hashes the UTF-8 bytes with SHA-256. Clients do not compute this version themselves.

This is Linha's documented encoding; it is not a claim of RFC 8785 numeric canonicalization. Submission replay uses PostgreSQL JSONB equality and the accepted result policy. Public request IDs are opaque identifiers, not hashes.

docs.title: Result identity
docs.text:
Results carry kind, schema and version. A typed restored handle rejects a descriptor mismatch before decoding. Files and parts include size and SHA-256. Dataset pages are ordered by relative path with opaque cursors; callers use those returned paths rather than deriving object keys.

Path templates expand the original acceptance time in UTC and require separate request and attempt identity segments. Persisted allocations make lost-response replay safe and reject overlapping or stale-attempt output.

docs.title: Executable contract fixtures
docs.text: The repository's API fixtures cover raw/typed equivalence, Unicode escaping, configuration hashing, Pod merging, path/date expansion, descriptors and cross-language limits. Go/JVM suites consume these fixtures; PostgreSQL tests exercise actual idempotency and allocation state.

docs.title: Run your first job
docs.text: In this tutorial you will build Linha, submit raw and typed jobs, restart the processes, and retrieve the original results. The fixture uses a lightweight JVM worker rather than Spark, so no Kubernetes cluster is required.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: Install Git, Go 1.27.1, Java 17, Maven 3.9.9, Node.js 22.12+ with npm, Python 3 and Docker. Docker must be running and your account must be able to start containers. Allow the fixture to download the PostgreSQL image. See the compatibility matrix for the pinned engine dependencies.

docs.title: 1. Get the source
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/k3rnL/linha.git
cd linha
java -version

The Java command should report Java 17. Select a Java 17 installation using JAVA_HOME if your machine has several versions.

docs.title: 2. Build the server and SDKs
docs.text:
mvn -B install
make build

Maven installs the SDK binaries and source JARs in your local Maven repository. make build builds the console and embeds it in bin/linha-server. Check it:

bin/linha-server --version

docs.title: 3. Submit jobs and retrieve their results
docs.text:
python3 scripts/e2e.py

The fixture starts PostgreSQL and Linha, submits requests through the JVM client, then starts the worker. It checks JSON results, file results and a failing result callback. Successful output contains two PASS: lines covering persisted diagnostics and raw/typed jobs, file output and restart retrieval. A nonzero exit code means one of its assertions failed.

The fixture explicitly disables authentication for its local processes. It does not change any existing deployment or use a permanent database.

docs.title: 4. Verify retrieval across restarts
docs.text:
The same fixture restarts the client, server and worker and retrieves results using the original identifiers. A successful run confirms that acceptance and retained result metadata survive those process restarts. The script removes the containers and temporary result directory when it finishes.

You now have a working server and locally installed SDKs. Continue with writing client and worker code, or deploy on Kubernetes to run the Spark engine.

docs.title: Publish a Linha release
docs.text: A version tag starts the release workflow. After validation, it publishes server and example-worker images to GHCR and signed SDK artifacts to Maven Central. This guide is for maintainers with publishing access.

docs.title: 1. Configure public metadata
docs.text:
Keep release-metadata.json, all Maven POMs and the license aligned with the public repository and verified Maven namespace. Linha uses k3rnL/linha, com.k3rnl and Apache-2.0.

The published parent is com.k3rnl:linha-jvm; the Scala 2.12 modules are linha-protocol_2.12, linha-client_2.12, linha-worker_2.12 and linha-spark_2.12 and linha-hadoop_2.12. Examples are packaged for the worker image and excluded from Central. Each SDK publication includes binary, sources, API documentation, checksums and signatures.

docs.title: 2. Configure the release environment
docs.text:
Create a GitHub Actions environment named release and set:

Secret Value MAVEN_CENTRAL_USERNAME Central Publisher Portal user-token username MAVEN_CENTRAL_PASSWORD Matching user-token password GPG_PRIVATE_KEY Complete ASCII-armored private signing-key export GPG_PASSPHRASE Its passphrase

The Central account must have publishing access to com.k3rnl. These are Portal token credentials, not an account login password. Maven uses server ID central. A key listing is not a private-key export.

Set secrets interactively through GitHub or gh secret set. To transfer a key without printing it or placing it in the repository:

set -o pipefail
gpg --armor --export-secret-keys YOUR_SIGNING_KEY_FINGERPRINT   | gh secret set GPG_PRIVATE_KEY --env release --repo k3rnL/linha

Publish the public key through a Central-supported keyserver. See Sonatype's Maven publishing and signature requirements.

GHCR uses GITHUB_TOKEN; only the image job requests packages: write. No separate registry PAT is needed.

docs.title: 3. Validate locally
docs.text:
Use Java 17 and Maven 3.9.9. Run the project checks, then rehearse publication:

python3 scripts/test-release.py
python3 scripts/check-release-artifacts.py

The rehearsal builds in a temporary workspace with disposable signing keys and a loopback Portal fixture. It checks SDK/source/API-documentation artifacts, checksums and signatures without publishing to Central.

docs.title: 4. Prepare and push the tag
docs.text:
Choose a new immutable version; do not reuse a published version. Align the root/module development versions, commit the code and validate the planned tag:

python3 scripts/prepare-release.py --check   --tag vX.Y.Z --repository k3rnL/linha
git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m 'Linha X.Y.Z'
git push origin vX.Y.Z

Replace X.Y.Z with the version matching the development POMs. Prerelease tags such as vX.Y.Z-rc.1 are supported. A tag push is the publication action. The workflow changes metadata only in its disposable workspace and waits for Central to report publication.

Images receive version and sha-<commit> tags, with no implicit latest image:

ghcr.io/k3rnl/linha/server:X.Y.Z
ghcr.io/k3rnl/linha/spark-example:X.Y.Z

The initial image platform is Linux amd64. The chart is packaged with the release. The separate documentation workflow captures a versioned site snapshot when a new release tag is published.

docs.title: Recover a failed job
docs.text:
GHCR and Central publication are independent. Inspect the affected registry or Portal deployment before rerunning failed jobs. An SDK timeout can occur after Central accepted the bundle. Finish an already accepted valid deployment rather than republishing an immutable version. Retry an image-only failure without rerunning a successful SDK publication.

Do not move a published tag. A code or metadata correction requires a new version. External registry permissions, namespace access and signing-key discovery still need verification in the hosted environment.

docs.title: Result expiry and physical cleanup
docs.text:
A job ID identifies durable metadata. Result retention controls how long its payload remains available. These lifetimes are separate: an expired payload does not erase status, attempt history, completion receipts or idempotency records.

Expiry is enforced at retrieval even when physical cleanup is disabled. results.cleanup.enabled is an independent opt-in deletion policy. Eligible allocations must belong to terminal attempts and be unprotected by a retained result, delegated writer or grace period.

Cleanup uses persisted allocation identity, not a scan of arbitrary user roots or buckets. Repeated sweeps tolerate partial failures. S3 object versions, backups and filesystem snapshots remain subject to external policies.

Set external storage lifecycle rules so they do not remove retained payloads before Linha's promised period. A missing object retains its metadata and returns an explicit storage failure; it is not silently treated as an empty result.

For the configuration and operational steps, see bound storage and enable cleanup.

docs.title: Scala/JVM SDK reference
docs.text:
All Scala artifacts use binary version 2.12 and Java 17. This guide uses SDK version 0.1.3-SNAPSHOT.

Build from source to use these development coordinates, or select the published 0.1.3 version from Maven Central.

Maven artifact Responsibility com.k3rnl:linha-protocol_2.12 Wire contracts, codecs, credentials and result paths com.k3rnl:linha-client_2.12 Client, contexts, job handles and OAuth acquisition com.k3rnl:linha-worker_2.12 Handler runtime, leases, progress and publication com.k3rnl:linha-hadoop_2.12 Scoped application filesystem with range reads com.k3rnl:linha-spark_2.12 SparkContext sessions and distributed result helpers

docs.title: Dependency declarations
docs.text:
For an SBT application that includes both client and worker examples:

scalaVersion := "2.12.20"
val linhaVersion = "0.1.3-SNAPSHOT"
libraryDependencies ++= Seq(
  "com.k3rnl" %% "linha-client" % linhaVersion,
  "com.k3rnl" %% "linha-spark" % linhaVersion,
  "org.apache.spark" %% "spark-sql" % "3.5.6" % Provided
)

The Spark module brings the worker/protocol SDKs transitively. A client-only application needs only linha-client; a shared entrypoint module also needs the Spark types used by its code. Spark is provided at runtime by the worker image. For Maven, use the explicit artifact names in the table, with group com.k3rnl.

docs.title: Client and context
docs.text:
Method Result / purpose new LinhaClient(url, credentials) Process-owned client; requires an ExecutionContext ensureBackend(name, spec) Future[LinhaContext]; attach to the derived configuration version restoreContext(id) Future[LinhaContext]; attach to an existing version job(id, codec) Typed handle; independent of engine lifetime rawJob(id) Untyped handle list(contextId, state, cursor, limit) Owner-scoped paginated jobs; limit defaults to 50 close() Release attachments and stop client lease scheduling context.submit(entrypoint, idempotencyKey, maxAttempts) Typed handle; defaults: generated key, one attempt context.submitRaw(RawRequest(...), idempotencyKey, maxAttempts) Same protocol with raw JSON parameters context.storage(destination) Live client session for an enabled application destination context.status() Current version state context.close() Release this context handle; shared handles retain their lease

Submission futures finish after durable acceptance, not job execution.

docs.title: Job handles
docs.text:
Method Purpose status() Job state, progress and failure attempts() Persisted execution history and diagnostics cancel() Commit cancellation intent resultMetadata() Retained result descriptor and file/dataset metadata result() Typed result; available after success, schema checked before decode parts(cursor, limit) Dataset part page; defaults to 100 download(allocationId, destination) Stream a retained file through the API downloadPart(partPath, destination) Stream a retained dataset part

result() does not poll until success. Download destinations must not already exist because the implementation uses Files.copy without replacement.

docs.title: OAuth credentials
docs.text:
CredentialProviders.oauthClientCredentials(tokenEndpoint, clientId, clientSecret, scopes, options, clock) returns a CredentialProvider.

Argument / option Default Contract tokenEndpoint required Absolute HTTPS token endpoint; no embedded credentials or fragment clientId required OAuth service client identifier clientSecret required () => String, evaluated on acquisition scopes empty sequence Optional OAuth scopes caFile none PEM trust file for this identity HTTP client insecureSkipVerify false Per-client certificate and hostname bypass allowHttp false Permit HTTP in an isolated fixture connectTimeout 5 seconds Connection deadline requestTimeout 10 seconds Whole response deadline, including body maxResponseBytes 1 MiB Bounded provider response clock UTC system clock Expiry calculation; injectable for tests

Token responses require token_type: Bearer and positive expires_in. Redirects are rejected. Response bodies and credentials are not included in CredentialException; the optional HTTP status is retained.

CredentialProvider.fileSecret(path) supplies a mounted client secret and rereads it on acquisition. CredentialProvider.none is for explicitly anonymous installations. A custom CredentialProvider can integrate application-owned token acquisition; OAuth client credentials is the bundled acquisition flow.

docs.title: Entrypoints and worker context
docs.text:
LinhaEntrypoint[R, E] exposes execute(LinhaJobContext[E]): R. SparkEntrypoint[R] specializes it for the Spark engine. Register an EntrypointCodec.derived[J, R](handler, version) in the worker image.

Context member Purpose jobId, attemptId Durable job identity and current attempt engine / Spark spark extension Engine object / request SparkSession progress(fraction, message) Persist progress in the current attempt isCancelled, checkCancelled() Cooperative cancellation results Storage-policy result writer onCleanup(action) Request-scoped cleanup callback Spark cache(frame) Reference-counted request-owned cache Spark broadcast(value) Broadcast destroyed with request cleanup

Worker bootstrap uses LinhaWorker.projectedIdentity() and projectedCredentials() for managed instance authentication. These internal worker credentials are separate from the application's OAuth credentials.

docs.title: Result types and paths
docs.text:
Type/helper Purpose Ordinary case class Encoded JSON result FileResult Registered immutable file descriptors DatasetResult Distributed parts and manifest results.stream(name, contentType)(write) Bounded byte stream results.file(name, contentType)(write) Temporary seekable Path Spark results.parquet(frame, name, partitionBy) Distributed Parquet ResultStorage.Local(root) Local backend result policy ResultStorage.S3(destination, path) S3 alias and declarative ResultPath ResultPath.template(text) Validated version-1 path template

See client/worker tutorial, result guide and path reference for examples.

Application file access and Unit/StatusResult completion are described in Application storage.

docs.title: Validation scope
docs.text: Linha has unit, database, JVM, browser, chart and disposable-cluster checks. This page distinguishes tested behavior from deployment assumptions. Run logs and environment-specific identifiers are local/CI artifacts, not public documentation.

docs.title: Test surfaces
docs.text:
Surface Covered behavior Go + PostgreSQL Durable acceptance, idempotency, ownership, leases, retries, cancellation, migrations and publication JVM SDK Codecs, transport, credential refresh, raw/typed dispatch, result helpers and diagnostics Process restart smoke Original job IDs and retained results after client/server/worker restarts Spark/Kind SparkApplications, concurrent requests, driver replacement, allocation, templates and result mounts Browser Login/session/role boundaries, navigation, replay, cancellation, previews and current/history views Prometheus/Grafana Metric contracts, deduplication, resets, outages, stale observations and dashboard expressions Helm Defaults, Secret references, namespace RBAC, UI ingress and optional monitoring resources Release rehearsal Metadata, signed SDK bundles, sources, API docs and checksum validation

See acceptance coverage, admin/observability measurements and recorded fixture measurements.

docs.title: Reproduce the routine checks
docs.text:
make check
mvn -B verify
make frontend-check
python3 scripts/e2e.py
python3 scripts/check-public-content.py

Set LINHA_TEST_DATABASE to a disposable PostgreSQL database for integration checks; otherwise those scenarios are explicitly skipped. Tests create/remove isolated schemas.

LINHA_TEST_DATABASE='postgres://user:password@localhost/linha_test?sslmode=disable'   go test -race -count=1 ./server/...

The CI workflow supplies its database fixture and runs the contract, chart, publication, browser and restart suites. Cluster fixtures are separate; see run disposable Kubernetes validation.

docs.title: Limits of the evidence
docs.text:
Single-host Kind tests establish application coordination and recovery, not multi-node database, object-store or filesystem HA. Production IAM, admission policy, storage failures and capacity need tests in the target environment. Measured fixture latency is not an SLO or a maximum throughput guarantee.

The current database schema is 12. Older binaries can reject it; retaining IDs during migration does not make arbitrary binary rollback safe. Job metadata is retained indefinitely; payload retention and cleanup are separately configured.

docs.title: Queue recovery and browser renewal
docs.text:
Disposable PostgreSQL and signed HTTPS OIDC fixtures verify pending-request moves, original IDs and idempotency, immutable payload/result policy, repeated move audit, claim races, retry backoff, compatibility rejection, transaction rollback and cross-pool visibility. Refresh tests cover concurrent rotation across independent pools, encrypted credentials, changed membership and token bindings, UserInfo, transient provider failures, nonrenewable expiry and logout.

Browser tests cover global and context-version selection, cancellation and moves, partial outcomes, viewer restrictions, searchable context suggestions, local date conversion and selection reset. These checks use local Docker fixtures; they do not assert deployment into an external Kubernetes cluster.

docs.title: Manage Spark applications
docs.text:
Configure driver capacity, executor allocation and Spark resources in the backend spec passed to ensureBackend. Linha creates one SparkApplication per managed driver. Kubeflow Spark Operator submits it, and Spark creates driver/executor Pods.

This guide assumes the operator watches the Linha namespace and your worker image contains the declared JVM main class and JAR. See deployment.

New driver Pods use <context-name>-<instance-id>-driver, for example reporting-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef-driver. Linha lowercases the context prefix, replaces unsupported characters with hyphens and limits that prefix to 23 characters, keeping the complete unique instance ID within Kubernetes' 63-character name limit. A name with no supported characters uses context as its prefix. Existing applications retain their current driver names until a new instance is provisioned. No client configuration change is needed.

docs.title: Set the application and resources
docs.text:
{
  "image": "registry.example/workers/reporting:1",
  "engine": {
    "type": "spark",
    "version": "3.5.6",
    "settings": {
      "application": {
        "mainClass": "example.WorkerMain",
        "mainApplicationFile": "local:///opt/linha/worker.jar"
      },
      "drivers": {
        "minDrivers": 1,
        "maxDrivers": 3,
        "maxConcurrentRequestsPerDriver": 2,
        "cores": 2,
        "coreRequest": "1",
        "coreLimit": "2",
        "memory": "10g",
        "memoryOverhead": "2g"
      },
      "executors": {
        "cores": 2,
        "memory": "4g",
        "memoryOverhead": "1g",
        "dynamicAllocation": true,
        "minExecutors": 0,
        "initialExecutors": 1,
        "maxExecutors": 8,
        "executorIdleTimeout": "60s",
        "cachedExecutorIdleTimeout": "120s",
        "shuffleTrackingTimeout": "120s"
      },
      "ui": {"enabled": true, "port": 4040}
    }
  },
  "results": {"type": "s3", "destination": "analytics"}
}

memory is the JVM heap, with memoryOverhead added to the container request and limit. A 10g heap plus 2g overhead gives the driver 12Gi. CPU requests and limits default to cores; override them separately when needed. Do not put -Xmx in javaOptions or override these resources through the main-container template. Defaults and bounds are in configuration reference.

The worker main method should use new SparkConf() to inherit submission configuration. Preserve Spark's driver/executor image entrypoint. Use application.arguments and javaOptions for application configuration, with Pod templates for files and environment variables.

docs.title: Tune the driver pool
docs.text:
Set minDrivers and maxDrivers for capacity bounds. Use maxConcurrentRequestsPerDriver to bound requests sharing one SparkContext. queueThreshold, waitSeconds and cooldownSeconds control driver growth; idleSeconds allows idle drivers above the minimum to retire.

Lost required drivers are replaced. With no live clients, the context version finishes accepted work and then stops all drivers, even when its minimum is positive. This lifetime behavior is described in architecture.

docs.title: Let idle executors retire
docs.text:
Enable dynamic allocation and set minExecutors: 0 if an idle application may have no executors. initialExecutors applies at startup; it is not a permanent minimum. Set finite cache and shuffle timeouts when their retained data should not keep executors indefinitely.

Default cache and shuffle timeouts are infinity. That is why an application can retain executors even after its visible jobs finish. Active tasks, cached blocks, shuffle tracking and the minimum count can delay executor removal. Finite retention can cause recomputation. Use ctx.cache and ctx.broadcast for request-owned resources; avoid globally clearing caches while other jobs run.

docs.title: Open a driver UI
docs.text:
Set ui.enabled: true, then choose a current driver:

kubectl -n linha get pods -l spark-role=driver
kubectl -n linha port-forward pod/<driver-pod-name> 4040:4040

Open http://localhost:4040. For ui.port: 4050, forward 4040:4050 instead. Each driver has its own UI and it disappears when that application stops.

The administrator console uses an ingress URL exposed by the SparkApplication when available. Linha creates no public Spark UI ingress or authentication proxy. The Spark UI is a separate service; configure its access policy separately. Use Spark event logs and a History Server for completed applications.

docs.title: Roll out a changed backend
docs.text:
Keep a logical name such as reporting. Ensure with the new image/settings and retain the returned context for the application process lifetime. Linha derives an immutable configuration version. Existing clients keep their version and accepted requests; new replicas attach to the new version. Close old contexts on graceful shutdown, or let their heartbeat expire after an unexpected exit.

Referenced ConfigMap and Secret contents do not enter the configuration hash. Use immutable names when a change must produce a new reproducible version. Only the primary worker image is resolved to a digest automatically; specify sidecar/init image digests yourself when required.

Read the upstream Spark configuration and SparkApplication guide for the engine-side behavior.

docs.title: Build a Scala client and worker
docs.text: This tutorial creates a Spark job, registers it in a worker, submits it through the client SDK, and restores its result using the saved job ID.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Use Java 17, Scala 2.12 and the matching com.k3rnl client, worker and Spark artifacts listed in the SDK reference.

Build the development SDKs with Java 17 mvn -B install.

You need a Linha deployment, Kubeflow Spark Operator and a worker registry that the deployment permits. Configure an S3 result destination named analytics and working server AWS credentials. Set up OAuth credentials for your application first.

The example uses a JSON result. File and dataset output uses the same submission flow.

docs.title: 1. Define the shared entrypoint
docs.text:
Put this code in a module shared by your client and worker:

package example

import linha._
import linha.json._
import linha.spark._
import linha.spark.syntax._

final case class RowsCount(value: Long)
final case class CountRows(size: Long) extends SparkEntrypoint[RowsCount] {
  def execute(ctx: LinhaJobContext[Spark]): RowsCount = {
    require(size >= 0)
    ctx.progress(0.1, "Counting rows")
    val count = ctx.spark.range(size).count()
    ctx.progress(1.0, "Finished")
    RowsCount(count)
  }
}
object CountRows {
  implicit val codec: EntrypointCodec[CountRows, RowsCount] =
    EntrypointCodec.derived("count-rows", 1)
}

The codec gives this business operation a stable handler name and wire version. The worker executes the class from its image; no class or closure is sent by the client. Compile this module before continuing.

docs.title: 2. Register the worker
docs.text:
package example

import linha.spark.SparkRuntime
import linha.worker.LinhaWorker
import org.apache.spark.SparkConf

object WorkerMain {
  def main(args: Array[String]): Unit = {
    val runtime = new SparkRuntime(new SparkConf(), sys.env("LINHA_CAPACITY").toInt)
    val worker = runtime.worker(
      sys.env("LINHA_SERVER_URL"),
      LinhaWorker.projectedIdentity(),
      Some(LinhaWorker.projectedCredentials())
    ).register(CountRows.codec)
    sys.addShutdownHook { worker.close(); runtime.close() }
    try worker.run()
    finally { worker.close(); runtime.close() }
  }
}

Package this main class and its dependencies into your worker JAR. The image must contain Spark 3.5.6 with Scala 2.12 and retain Spark's native container entrypoint. Place the JAR at /opt/linha/worker.jar, or update the application path below. The repository's example worker provides a runnable assembly and Dockerfile.

Push your image and verify that its repository is in Linha's allowedImages. Use compatible dependency shading: see compatibility.

docs.title: 3. Create the application client
docs.text:
import linha.CredentialProvider
import linha.client.LinhaClient
import linha.client.auth.CredentialProviders
import java.nio.file.Paths
import scala.concurrent.ExecutionContext.Implicits.global

val credentials = CredentialProviders.oauthClientCredentials(
  "https://identity.example/realms/jobs/protocol/openid-connect/token",
  "reporting-api",
  CredentialProvider.fileSecret(Paths.get("/credentials/client-secret"))
)
val client = new LinhaClient("https://linha.example", credentials)

Keep this client for the application's process lifetime. The mounted file contains an OAuth client secret; the SDK acquires the access token.

docs.title: 4. Ensure a context and submit
docs.text:
import example.{CountRows, RowsCount}
import io.circe.parser.parse
import scala.concurrent.Await
import scala.concurrent.duration._

val spec = parse("""{
  "image": "registry.example/workers/reporting:1",
  "engine": {"type":"spark","version":"3.5.6","settings":{
    "application":{"mainClass":"example.WorkerMain",
      "mainApplicationFile":"local:///opt/linha/worker.jar"},
    "drivers":{"minDrivers":1,"maxDrivers":2,
      "maxConcurrentRequestsPerDriver":2,
      "memory":"1g","memoryOverhead":"512m","cores":1},
    "executors":{"dynamicAllocation":true,"minExecutors":0,
      "initialExecutors":1,"maxExecutors":4,
      "memory":"2g","memoryOverhead":"512m","cores":1,
      "executorIdleTimeout":"60s","cachedExecutorIdleTimeout":"120s",
      "shuffleTrackingTimeout":"120s"}
  }},
  "results":{"type":"s3","destination":"analytics"}
}""").fold(throw _, identity)

val context = Await.result(client.ensureBackend("reporting", spec), 30.seconds)
val handle = Await.result(
  context.submit(CountRows(1000), idempotencyKey = "request-42"),
  30.seconds
)
println(handle.id)

Return handle.id to your API caller. The ID is durable; Spark processing may start later. The ensure operation can resolve an image and validate settings, whereas job acceptance waits only for its database transaction.

Keep the context while this process serves requests. Reuse the same name after configuration changes; Linha derives a version. Use a fresh business idempotency key for each new request, and reuse it when retrying the same acceptance.

docs.title: 5. Poll and retrieve
docs.text:
val state = Await.result(handle.status(), 10.seconds)
println(state)

Poll at your chosen interval until the state is SUCCEEDED, FAILED or CANCELLED. After success:

val result: RowsCount = Await.result(handle.result(), 30.seconds)
println(result.value) // 1000

result() retrieves an available result; it does not wait for execution. Use handle.attempts() to inspect persisted failures and handle.cancel() to request cancellation.

docs.title: 6. Restore the handle later
docs.text:
Create a new client with the same application identity and restore by ID:

val restored = client.job(savedJobId, CountRows.codec)
val retained = Await.result(restored.result(), 30.seconds)

This operation needs no active context or running driver. On application shutdown, close the context and client after stopping acceptance of new application requests:

context.close()
client.close()

Accepted work drains before Linha stops an unused context version. For the equivalent raw JSON route, see HTTP API.

docs.title: Release notes
docs.text:
Release notes describe the behavior captured by each tag. Use the documentation version selector for releases published after the versioned site was introduced. Older release tags are not rebuilt automatically into new documentation snapshots.

  • 0.1.3: OAuth clients, application storage, queue recovery and renewable console sessions.
  • 0.1.2: reduce retired-resource Kubernetes API traffic.
  • 0.1.1: configurable provider TLS verification and simpler admin rules.
  • 0.1.0: initial durable job service, Scala/JVM SDKs, managed Spark engine, administrator console and Prometheus/Grafana integration.

Development pages can describe features absent from older artifacts. Do not apply new SDK examples to an older binary solely because its version is listed here.

docs.title: Linha 0.1.1
docs.text: Linha 0.1.1 adds configurable identity-provider HTTPS verification and simplifies administrator membership rules.

docs.title: Changes
docs.text:
• security.oidc.tls.insecureSkipVerify and its environment equivalent default to false and apply only to identity discovery, signing keys and browser token exchange. Signature, issuer, audience, expiry, nonce and membership checks remain.
  • Viewer/operator rules inherit the configured browser issuer. Repeating it is optional; a conflicting issuer is rejected.
  • CI regenerates temporary fixture output instead of relying on cached test success, and pins Maven 3.9.9 for deterministic Central bundles.

docs.title: Upgrade
docs.text:
Update the server image and chart together to 0.1.1. No database migration or worker protocol change is required. Certificate bypass is optional; trusting the provider CA keeps TLS verification enabled. The server's setting does not change browser certificate trust.

This is a historical release. Current API/browser authentication fields differ; use the documentation captured with the version you deploy.

docs.title: Artifacts and verification
docs.text:
Images are ghcr.io/k3rnl/linha/server:0.1.1 and ghcr.io/k3rnl/linha/spark-example:0.1.1. JVM artifacts use com.k3rnl, version 0.1.1, with sources, API documentation and signatures. The release includes the Helm chart and checksum.

Validation covered Go/PostgreSQL tests and race checks, browser sessions, Java 17 JVM builds, chart configuration, formatting, release preparation and specification validation. See the release comparison.

docs.title: Linha 0.1.2
docs.text: Linha 0.1.2 reduces Kubernetes API traffic from already deleted resources in retired context history.

docs.title: Changes
docs.text:
• Stop per-name probes for stopped contexts and dead instances.
  • Inventory managed Pods, Services and SparkApplications once per minute per server, including startup. An empty two-replica deployment needs six collection calls per minute, independent of retained history.
  • Preserve cleanup of late creates and leftover Services using persisted intent, reconciliation ownership and UID-conditional deletion.
  • Bound retries after inventory/deletion failure without interrupting active capacity, accepted-work draining, reactivation or retained results.

docs.title: Upgrade
docs.text:
Update every server replica to 0.1.2. This change needs no database migration, additional RBAC, SDK upgrade or business worker rebuild. Older replicas keep the previous polling behavior until replaced. Late orphan cleanup can wait until the next successful minute sweep.

The unreleased OAuth SDK and independent API/browser configuration described in development documentation are not part of this release.

docs.title: Artifacts and verification
docs.text:
Images are ghcr.io/k3rnl/linha/server:0.1.2 and ghcr.io/k3rnl/linha/spark-example:0.1.2. JVM artifacts use com.k3rnl, version 0.1.2, with sources, API documentation and signatures. The release includes the Helm chart and checksum.

A fixture with 5,000 dead records and 100 controller ticks performs three inventory requests with no per-name probes. Tests also cover pagination, UID checks, competing controllers, late creation, failure backoff and reactivation. Go/PostgreSQL/race, JVM, restart and specification checks passed. See the release comparison.

docs.title: Linha 0.1.3
docs.text: Linha 0.1.3 adds renewable application credentials, storage access for workers, and administrative tools for recovering queues stranded on an unusable context.

docs.title: Changes
docs.text:
• OAuth 2.0 client credentials in the JVM SDK, with expiry-aware concurrent token renewal. Public API JWT authentication and browser OIDC have independent settings.
  • Configurable browser OIDC scopes and clearer administrator membership diagnostics.
  • Application storage through explicitly authorized Linha destinations, scoped client/worker sessions, reusable resource locks and a new Hadoop filesystem SDK. Provider storage credentials stay on the server.
  • Status-only jobs that finish without allocating a managed result file.
  • Batch cancellation and movement of queued or retrying requests to a compatible context version, preserving request IDs, payloads, retry history and result policy.
  • Searchable context filters, local date/time inputs, page selection and centered confirmation dialogs in both global and context request views.
  • Encrypted OIDC refresh credentials shared across server replicas. Refreshed identity and group membership remain authoritative within the configured session lifetime.
  • Context-readable Spark driver names with full unique instance IDs, and a writable Ivy directory for Spark images running with arbitrary container UIDs.
  • A statically linked server binary validated inside its runtime image.
  • Standalone, searchable documentation with version snapshots on GitHub Pages.

docs.title: Upgrade
docs.text:
This release changes authentication configuration. Configure API validation under security.api and browser login under security.oidc; administrator rules remain under security.admin. Application clients use OAuth client credentials and mount only their client secret when needed. See client authentication and administrator setup.

Back up PostgreSQL and stop the old server replicas before deploying all 0.1.3 replicas. Startup migrates the database to schema 12. Older binaries reject newer schemas; binary rollback requires restoring a compatible database backup. Requests and published result metadata remain durable across the upgrade.

Use matching 0.1.3 SDKs when rebuilding application clients and worker images. Application storage requires explicit destination opt-in and adequate server bandwidth and staging space. Application dataset files have a separate lifecycle from retained job results. See application storage.

Sign in again to obtain browser refresh credentials. Providers must issue refresh tokens; the absolute ui.sessionSeconds limit still applies. Existing Spark drivers retain their names until replaced, when the readable naming convention takes effect.

docs.title: Artifacts and validation
docs.text:
Images are ghcr.io/k3rnl/linha/server:0.1.3 and ghcr.io/k3rnl/linha/spark-example:0.1.3. Maven artifacts use com.k3rnl, version 0.1.3: the parent plus protocol, client, worker, Spark and Hadoop SDK modules, with sources, API documentation, checksums and signatures. The GitHub release also includes the Helm chart and its checksum.

Validation covers Go/PostgreSQL and race checks, JVM SDKs, browser interactions, chart rendering, restart recovery, OpenAPI contracts, signed publication bundles and documentation builds. Hosted release workflows validate the tagged commit before publishing. External cluster and provider deployment policies still need validation in the target environment.

See the release comparison.

docs.title: Recorded fixture measurements
docs.text: The September 30 platform run used one Kind host, two allowed drivers, one request slot per driver and 0–2 one-core executors per driver. Both roles used 512m heap plus 384m overhead. Executor idle/cache/shuffle timeouts were 5s/8s/8s; driver idle was 120s.

docs.title: Measurements
docs.text:
Observation Recorded value Durable acceptance, seven submissions 2.96–4.99 ms Four load-job queue waits 7.44s, 7.47s, 37.84s, 38.04s Peak drivers / executors / simultaneous requests 2 / 4 / 2 Retained request RDDs after completion 0 Additional wait for executor retirement after the UI/cache check 4.24s Additional wait for idle driver retirement after later checks 107.44s

Polling began after other checks, so these retirement observations are not exact time from the final Spark task. They are fixture measurements, not capacity or latency promises.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
PostgreSQL/S3 restarts, API replica replacement and complete driver shutdown preserved local/S3 result access. Signed-token tests checked cryptographic identity rules separately. The fixture did not certify production IAM, multi-node storage failure or load at result-size/part-count ceilings.

Executable groups include e2e.py, platform-results-e2e.py, platform-fault-e2e.py, platform-load-e2e.py, platform-final-smoke.py, pod-template-e2e.py and test-helm.py. See validation scope and acceptance coverage.

Generated request IDs, image digests and raw run logs stay outside Git. CI can retain them as run artifacts when needed.
